title.zh: 卷三百八十九 列傳第一百四十八 尤袤 謝諤 顏師魯 袁樞 李椿 劉儀鳳 張孝祥
title.en: Volume 389 Biographies 148: You Mao, Xie E, Yan Shilu, Yuan Shu, Li Chun, Liu Yifeng, Zhang Xiaoxiang
title.raw: 卷三百八十九 列傳第一百四十八 尤袤 謝諤 顏師魯 袁樞 李椿 劉儀鳳 張孝祥 Volume 389 Biographies 148: You Mao, Xie E, Yan Shilu, Yuan Shu, Li Chun, Liu Yifeng, Zhang Xiaoxiang

sentences.zh: 尤袤 謝諤 顏師魯 袁樞 李椿 劉儀鳳 張孝祥

translations.literal: You Mao, Xie E, Yan Shilu, Yuan Shu, Li Chun, Liu Yifeng, Zhang Xiaoxiang
translations.idiomatic: You Mao, Xie E, Yan Shilu, Yuan Shu, Li Chun, Liu Yifeng, and Zhang Xiaoxiang

sentences.zh: 尤袤，字延之，常州無錫人。

translations.literal: You Mao, courtesy name Yanzhi, was a native of Wuxi in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: You Mao, whose courtesy name was Yanzhi, came from Wuxi in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 少穎異，蔣偕、施坰呼為奇童。

translations.literal: In youth he was exceptionally bright; Jiang Xie and Shi Qiu called him a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he showed unusual brilliance, and Jiang Xie and Shi Qiu hailed him as a wonder-child.

sentences.zh: 入太學，以詞賦冠多士，尋冠南宮。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University, took first place among the students in rhapsody and fu composition, and soon topped the civil examination at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the Imperial University he led his peers in rhapsody and fu, and soon afterward ranked first in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 紹興十八年，擢進士第。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Shaoxing he was selected in the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: In 1148 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 嘗為泰興令，問民疾苦，皆曰：「邵伯鎮置頓，為金使經行也，使率不受而空厲民。

translations.literal: He once served as magistrate of Taixing; when he asked about the people's hardships, all said: "The rest station set up at Shaobo garrison is for the passage of Jin envoys; the envoys habitually refuse payment yet empty the people nonetheless.
translations.idiomatic: While magistrate of Taixing he inquired into local hardships; everyone told him that the relay post at Shaobo garrison existed for Jin envoys on the road, who routinely took nothing with them yet still drained the people dry.

sentences.zh: 漕司輸槁秸，致一束數十金。

translations.literal: The transport office delivered straw fodder, so that a single bundle cost dozens of cash in gold.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner supplied straw fodder at such cost that a single bundle ran to dozens of strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 二弊久莫之去。」

translations.literal: These two abuses had long gone unremoved."
translations.idiomatic: These two abuses had persisted for years with no one able to abolish them.

sentences.zh: 乃力請台閫奏免之。

translations.literal: He then pressed the circuit and commandery authorities to memorialize for their abolition.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed the regional authorities to memorialize the throne and have both practices abolished.

sentences.zh: 縣舊有外城，屢殘於寇，頹毀甚，袤即修築。

translations.literal: The county had long had an outer wall, repeatedly damaged by raiders and badly ruined; Mao immediately repaired and built it up.
translations.idiomatic: The county still had an outer wall that bandits had battered again and again until it lay in ruins; Mao set about rebuilding it at once.

sentences.zh: 已而金渝盟，陷揚州，獨泰興以有城得全。

translations.literal: Before long the Jin violated the treaty, captured Yangzhou, and Taixing alone escaped destruction because it had walls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Jin broke the treaty and took Yangzhou, yet Taixing alone survived intact thanks to its fortifications.

sentences.zh: 後因事至舊治，吏民羅拜曰：「此吾父母也。」

translations.literal: Later, when on business he returned to his former jurisdiction, officials and people lined up to bow and said: "This is our father and mother."
translations.idiomatic: When he later returned on official business, clerks and commoners lined the road to bow and cried, "Here is our father and mother!"

sentences.zh: 為立生祠。

translations.literal: They erected a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: They erected a shrine to him in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 注江陰學官，需次七年，為讀書計。

translations.literal: He was registered as an educational officer at Jiangyin and waited seven years in queue, planning to devote himself to study.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as an educational officer at Jiangyin, he spent seven years awaiting appointment so that he could devote himself to reading.

sentences.zh: 從臣以靖退薦，召除將作監簿。

translations.literal: Attendant officials recommended him for his quiet withdrawal; he was summoned and appointed Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials recommended him for his retiring manner, and he was summoned to serve as registrar in the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 大宗正闕丞，人爭求之，陳俊卿曰：「當予不求者。」

translations.literal: The Imperial Clan Court lacked a vice director; men scrambled to obtain the post. Chen Junqing said: "It should go to one who does not seek it."
translations.idiomatic: When the vice directorship of the Imperial Clan Court fell vacant, everyone scrambled for it; Chen Junqing said, "Give it to the man who is not scrambling."

sentences.zh: 遂除袤。

translations.literal: Mao was then appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Mao received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 虞允文以史事過三館，問誰可為秘書丞者，僉以袤對，亟授之。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen, on historiographical business, passed through the Three Institutes and asked who could serve as secretary director; all answered with Mao, and he was promptly given the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yunwen passed through the Three Institutes on historiographical business and asked who might serve as secretary director, everyone named Mao, and the appointment followed at once.

sentences.zh: 張栻曰：「真秘書也。」

translations.literal: Zhang Shi said: "A true secretary director."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi remarked, "Now there is a real secretary director."

sentences.zh: 兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官，遷著作郎兼太子侍讀。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as compiler in the National History Office and collator in the Veritable Records Office, and was promoted to Compiler and Lecturer to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as compiler in the National History Office and collator in the Veritable Records Office, and was promoted to Compiler while lecturing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 先是，張栻說自閣門入西府，士論鼎沸，從臣因執奏而去者數十人，袤率三館上書諫，且不往見。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Shi entered the Western Secretariat through the Gate of Imperial Audience, scholarly opinion seethed; several dozen attendant officials resigned by memorializing their objections. Mao led the Three Institutes in a memorial of remonstrance and moreover refused to go see him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Shi entered the Western Secretariat through the Gate of Imperial Audience, opinion among scholars boiled over and dozens of attendant officials resigned in protest. Mao led the Three Institutes in a joint memorial of remonstrance and refused even to pay Zhang a visit.

sentences.zh: 後說留身密奏，於是梁克家罷相，袤與秘書少監陳騤各與郡。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Shi stayed behind and made a secret memorial; thereupon Liang Kejia was dismissed as chief councilor, and Mao and Vice Director of the Palace Library Chen Gui were each sent to a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang stayed behind for a secret audience; Liang Kejia was dismissed as chief councilor, and both Mao and Vice Director of the Palace Library Chen Gui were banished to prefectural posts.

sentences.zh: 袤得台州，州五縣，有丁無產者輸二年丁稅，凡萬有三千家。

translations.literal: Mao received Taizhou; in the prefecture's five counties, households with labor obligation but no property paid two years' labor tax, totaling more than thirteen thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was assigned to Taizhou, where in five counties more than thirteen thousand households with adult males but no land were paying two years' labor tax at once.

sentences.zh: 前守趙汝愚修郡城工才什三，屬袤成之。

translations.literal: The previous prefect Zhao Ruyu had carried the prefectural wall repair only three-tenths complete; Mao was charged to finish it.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor Zhao Ruyu had brought the prefectural wall only thirty percent toward completion, and Mao was told to finish the work.

sentences.zh: 袤按行前築，殊鹵莽，亟命更築，加高厚，數月而畢。

translations.literal: Mao inspected the earlier construction and found it quite crude; he immediately ordered rebuilding, adding height and thickness, and within months it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting what had been built, he found the work shockingly slipshod, ordered a full rebuild with added height and thickness, and finished within months.

sentences.zh: 明年大水，更築之，墉正直水沖，城賴以不沒。

translations.literal: The next year there was a great flood; the rebuilt wall stood square in the flood's path, and the city was spared inundation.
translations.idiomatic: The next year a great flood struck; the rebuilt wall took the brunt of the current head-on, and the city was saved from drowning.

sentences.zh: 會有毀袤者，上疑之，使人密察，民誦其善政不絕口，乃錄其《東湖》四詩歸奏。

translations.literal: It happened that someone slandered Mao; the emperor grew suspicious and sent men to investigate in secret. The people praised his good government without cease, so the investigators copied his four "Eastern Lake" poems and returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: When slander reached the emperor, he grew suspicious and sent agents to investigate in secret; the people could not stop praising Mao's governance, so the agents copied his four "Eastern Lake" poems and brought them back to court.

sentences.zh: 上讀而歎賞，遂以文字受知。

translations.literal: The emperor read them and sighed in admiration, and thereafter came to know him through his literary work.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read them with admiration and thereafter came to value Mao for his literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 除淮東提舉常平，改江東。

translations.literal: He was appointed Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries for Huaidong, then transferred to Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Huaidong, then transferred to Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 江東旱，單車行部，核一路常平米，通融有無，以之振貸。

translations.literal: Jiangdong suffered drought; he traveled the circuit alone in a single cart, audited the Ever-Normal grain along the route, pooled surplus and shortage, and used it for relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck Jiangdong he toured the circuit alone, audited Ever-Normal stores along the route, pooled surpluses and deficits, and used the grain for relief lending.

sentences.zh: 朱熹知南康，講荒政，下五等戶租五鬥以下悉蠲之，袤推行于諸郡，民無流殍。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi, as prefect of Nanchang, expounded famine policy and remitted all rent below five dou for fifth-class households; Mao extended this through the prefectures, and the people did not wander off to starve.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xi governed Nanchang he preached famine relief and remitted all rent below five dou for the poorest households; Mao spread the practice through the prefectures so that no one was driven to wander and starve.

sentences.zh: 進直秘閣，遷江西漕兼知隆興府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Attendant in the Privy Archives and transferred to Jiangxi transport commissioner while also governing Longxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant in the Privy Archives and made Jiangxi transport commissioner while also governing Longxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屢請祠，進直敷文閣，改江東提刑。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested a shrine appointment, was advanced to Attendant in the Hall for Spreading Literature, and was changed to Jiangdong judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After repeatedly requesting a sinecure post he was advanced to attendant in the Hall for Spreading Literature and transferred to judicial commissioner in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 梁克家薦袤及鄭僑以言事去國，久於外，當召，上可之。

translations.literal: Liang Kejia recommended Mao and Zheng Qiao, who had left the capital for remonstrating and long served outside; they ought to be summoned, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kejia recommended Mao and Zheng Qiao, who had left court after remonstrating and long served in the provinces; the emperor agreed they should be recalled.

sentences.zh: 召對，言：「水旱之備惟常平、義倉，願預飭有司隨市價禁科抑，則人自樂輸，必易集事。」

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he said: "Preparation for flood and drought rests solely in the Ever-Normal and Charity Granaries; I wish that responsible offices be instructed beforehand to follow market price and forbid forced collection and suppression, so that people will gladly contribute of themselves and the task will surely be easy to complete."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said, "Flood and drought preparedness depends on the Ever-Normal and Charity Granaries alone; instruct the responsible offices in advance to follow market prices and forbid forced levies and price suppression, and people will contribute willingly—the work will be easy to finish."

sentences.zh: 除吏部郎官、太子侍講，累遷樞密檢正兼左諭德。

translations.literal: He was appointed Department of Personnel bureau director and Lecturer to the Crown Prince, and was repeatedly promoted to Rectifier in the Bureau of Military Affairs while also serving as Left Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a bureau director in the Department of Personnel and lecturer to the crown prince, and rose step by step to rectifier in the Bureau of Military Affairs while also serving as left mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 輸對，又申言民貧兵怨者甚切。

translations.literal: In a submitted audience he again spoke urgently that the people's poverty and the soldiers' resentment were very severe.
translations.idiomatic: In a submitted audience he again spoke with great urgency of the people's poverty and the soldiers' resentment.

sentences.zh: 夏旱，詔求闕失，袤上封事，大略言：「天地之氣，宣通則和，壅遏則乖；

translations.literal: In a summer drought an edict sought oversights and failures; Mao submitted a sealed memorial, saying in outline: "The qi of Heaven and Earth, when communicated freely, is harmonious; when blocked and obstructed, it is discordant;
translations.idiomatic: During a summer drought the throne called for reports of oversights; Mao submitted a sealed memorial arguing in essence that Heaven and Earth's vital force flows harmoniously when unobstructed but turns discordant when blocked;

sentences.zh: 人心舒暢則悅，抑鬱則憤。

translations.literal: when the human heart is at ease it is pleased; when depressed it is resentful.
translations.idiomatic: that when hearts are at ease people are content, but when hearts are pent up they seethe with anger.

sentences.zh: 催科峻急而農民怨；

translations.literal: Tax collection is harsh and urgent, and the farmers resent it;
translations.idiomatic: Harsh tax collection breeds resentment among farmers;

sentences.zh: 關征苛察而商旅怨；

translations.literal: pass duties are exacting and scrutinizing, and merchants and travelers resent it;
translations.idiomatic: exacting tolls and levies breed resentment among merchants and travelers;

sentences.zh: 差注留滯，而士大夫有失職之怨；

translations.literal: appointments linger and stall, and scholar-officials have the resentment of lost office;
translations.idiomatic: stalled appointments breed resentment among scholar-officials who lose their posts;

sentences.zh: 廩給朘削，而士卒有不足之怨；

translations.literal: granary rations are pared down, and soldiers have the resentment of insufficiency;
translations.idiomatic: pared rations breed resentment among soldiers who go without enough;

sentences.zh: 奏讞不時報，百久系囚者怨；

translations.literal: trial memorials are not reported in season, and the resentment of long-imprisoned convicts;
translations.idiomatic: untimely rulings on cases breed resentment among prisoners long in chains;

sentences.zh: 幽枉不獲伸，而負累者怨；

translations.literal: hidden wrongs do not obtain redress, and those bearing false charges resent it;
translations.idiomatic: unredressed injustice breeds resentment among the falsely accused;

sentences.zh: 強暴殺人，多特貸命，使已死者怨；

translations.literal: violent men who kill people often receive commuted sentences, making the already dead resent it;
translations.idiomatic: commuted sentences for violent killers breed resentment even among the dead;

sentences.zh: 有司買納，不即酬價，負販者怨。

translations.literal: responsible offices purchase and levy goods but do not promptly pay the price, and petty traders resent it.
translations.idiomatic: delayed payment for goods the state requisitions breeds resentment among peddlers and small traders.

sentences.zh: 人心抑鬱所以感傷天和者，豈特一事而已。

translations.literal: The human heart's depression that thus injures Heaven's harmony—is it limited to a single matter alone?
translations.idiomatic: The human heart's pent-up grief that disturbs Heaven's harmony is hardly confined to any one cause alone.

sentences.zh: 方今救荒之策，莫急於勸分，輸納既多，朝廷吝於推賞。

translations.literal: At present in famine-relief policy nothing is more urgent than encouraging sharing; though contributions are already many, the court is stingy in extending rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Among famine policies today nothing is more urgent than encouraging mutual aid; though many have contributed, the court is reluctant to reward them.

sentences.zh: 乞詔有司檢舉行之。」

translations.literal: I beg that an edict instruct the responsible offices to investigate and carry this out."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty order the responsible offices to investigate and implement this."

sentences.zh: 高宗崩前一日，除太常少卿。

translations.literal: On the day before Gaozong's death he was appointed Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The day before Gaozong died, Mao was appointed vice minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 自南渡來，恤禮散失，事出倉卒，上下罔措，每有討論，悉付之袤，斟酌損益，便於今而不戾于古。

translations.literal: Since the move south across the river, mourning rites had been scattered and lost; matters arose in haste and above and below were at a loss. Whenever there was discussion, all was entrusted to Mao, who weighed additions and subtractions, convenient for the present without violating the ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court moved south, mourning rites had fallen into disarray; when Gaozong died everything happened in haste and no one knew what to do. Every question of ritual was left to Mao, who adjusted practice to suit the present without violating ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 當定廟號，袤與禮官定號「高宗」，洪邁獨請號「世祖」。

translations.literal: When the temple name was to be fixed, Mao and the ritual officials fixed the name "Gaozong"; Hong Mai alone requested the name "Shizu."
translations.idiomatic: When the temple name was to be decided, Mao and the ritual officials favored "Gaozong," while Hong Mai alone argued for "Shizu."

sentences.zh: 袤率禮官顏師魯、鄭僑奏曰：「宗廟之制，祖有功，宗有德。

translations.literal: Mao led the ritual officials Yan Shilu and Zheng Qiao in memorializing: "In the ancestral temple system, zu honors merit and zong honors virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Mao led the ritual officials Yan Shilu and Zheng Qiao in a memorial: "In the ancestral temple system, zu honors merit and zong honors virtue.

sentences.zh: 藝祖規創大業，為宋太祖，太宗混一區夏，為宋太宗，自真宗至欽宗，聖聖相傳，廟制一定，萬世不易。

translations.literal: Taizu planned and founded the great enterprise and is Song Taizu; Taizong unified the realm and is Song Taizong; from Zhenzong through Qinzong, sage succeeded sage, the temple system was once fixed and shall not change for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu planned and founded the great enterprise as Song Taizu; Taizong unified the realm as Song Taizong; from Zhenzong through Qinzong sage succeeded sage—the temple system was fixed once for all and must never change.

sentences.zh: 在禮，子為父屈，示有尊也。

translations.literal: In ritual, the son yields to the father, showing that there is honor due.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual the son yields to the father, showing where honor is due.

sentences.zh: 太上親為徽宗子，子為祖而父為宗，失昭穆之序。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor was personally a son of Huizong; to make the son zu and the father zong loses the order of zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor was Huizong's own son; to make the son zu and the father zong reverses the proper zhao-mu order.

sentences.zh: 議者不過以漢光武為比，光武以長沙王后，布衣崛起，不與哀、平相繼，其稱無嫌。

translations.literal: Those who argued did no more than compare him to Han Guangwu; Guangwu, after the Prince of Changsha, rose from common cloth and did not succeed Ai and Ping in succession—his title raised no objection.
translations.idiomatic: Advocates could only compare him to Han Guangwu, who rose from commoner status after the Prince of Changsha and did not succeed Emperors Ai and Ping directly—his title raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 太上中興，雖同光武，然實繼徽宗正統，以子繼父，非光武比。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor restored the dynasty—though like Guangwu, in fact he succeeded Huizong's orthodox line, a son succeeding a father, not comparable to Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor restored the dynasty; though the case resembles Guangwu's, he in fact continued Huizong's legitimate line as son succeeding father—not a parallel to Guangwu at all.

sentences.zh: 將來祔廟在徽宗下而稱祖，恐在天之靈有所不安。」

translations.literal: If in the future he is enshrined in the temple below Huizong yet called zu, I fear his spirit in Heaven will be ill at ease."
translations.idiomatic: If he is later enshrined below Huizong yet called zu, I fear his spirit in Heaven will not rest easy."

sentences.zh: 詔群臣集議，袤復上議如初，邁論遂屈。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to assemble for discussion; Mao again submitted his argument as at first, and Mai's position was thus overborne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministers to debate the matter; Mao restated his original argument, and Mai's position was defeated.

sentences.zh: 詔從禮官議。

translations.literal: An edict followed the ritual officials' proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed the ritual officials' view.

sentences.zh: 眾論紛然。

translations.literal: Public discussion was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion at court remained divided.

sentences.zh: 會禮部、太常寺亦同主「高宗」，謂本朝創業中興，皆在商丘，取「商高宗」，實為有證。

translations.literal: It happened that the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices also alike upheld "Gaozong," saying that this dynasty's founding and restoration both lay at Shangqiu, and taking "Shang Gaozong" was in fact well grounded.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices also backed "Gaozong," noting that both the dynasty's founding and its restoration were linked to Shangqiu and that the Shang ruler Gaozong offered genuine precedent.

sentences.zh: 始詔從初議。

translations.literal: Only then did an edict follow the initial proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did an edict adopt the original proposal.

sentences.zh: 建議事堂，令皇太子參決庶務。

translations.literal: It was proposed at the Council Chamber that the crown prince participate in deciding ordinary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the Council Chamber it was proposed that the crown prince take part in deciding routine affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 袤時兼侍讀，乃獻書，以為：「儲副之位，止於侍膳問安，不交外事；

translations.literal: Mao was then concurrently Lecturer and submitted a letter, holding: "The heir apparent's position is limited to attending meals and inquiring after health, and does not touch outside affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Mao, then also lecturing the heir apparent, submitted a letter arguing that the crown prince's proper role was limited to attending meals and inquiring after his father's health and should not extend to outside affairs;

sentences.zh: 撫軍監國，自漢至今，多出權宜。

translations.literal: commanding the army and overseeing the state, from Han to the present, has mostly arisen from expedient measures.
translations.idiomatic: that commanding armies and overseeing the realm, from Han times to the present, has almost always been an expedient born of crisis.

sentences.zh: 乞便懇辭以彰殿下之令德。」

translations.literal: I beg that he courteously decline at once to display His Highness's fine virtue."
translations.idiomatic: He begged the crown prince to decline promptly so as to display his own fine virtue."

sentences.zh: 台臣乞定喪制，袤奏：「釋老之教，矯誣褻瀆，非所以嚴宮禁、崇几筵，宜一切禁止。」

translations.literal: Censorate officials requested that mourning regulations be fixed; Mao memorialized: "The teachings of Buddhism and Daoism are deceptive fabrications and profane irreverence—not the means to tighten the palace precincts and honor the spirit tablets; they should all be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: When censors asked that mourning regulations be fixed, Mao memorialized that Buddhist and Daoist rites were deceptive and profane, unfit for tightening palace discipline and honoring the spirit tablets, and should be forbidden altogether.

sentences.zh: 靈駕將發引，忽定配享之議，洪邁請用呂頤浩、韓世忠、趙鼎、張俊。

translations.literal: As the imperial coffin was about to depart on the procession, the question of spirit tablets in joint worship was suddenly fixed; Hong Mai requested Lü Yihao, Han Shizhong, Zhao Ding, and Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the imperial coffin was about to leave the palace, the question of joint spirit-tablet worship was suddenly decided; Hong Mai proposed Lü Yihao, Han Shizhong, Zhao Ding, and Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 袤言：「祖宗典故，既祔然後議配享，今忽定於靈駕發引一日前，不集眾論，懼無以厭伏勳臣子孫之心。

translations.literal: Mao said: "According to ancestral precedent, joint worship is discussed only after enshrinement; now it is suddenly fixed one day before the coffin's departure, without gathering collective opinion—I fear this cannot satisfy the hearts of meritorious ministers' descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Mao objected that ancestral precedent called for debating joint worship only after enshrinement, yet the court had fixed the list a day before the procession without broad consultation, which might not satisfy the descendants of meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 宜反覆熟議，以俟論定。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to deliberate repeatedly and await settled opinion."
translations.idiomatic: He urged repeated deliberation until opinion settled.

sentences.zh: 奏入，詔未預議官詳議以聞，繼寢之，卒用四人者。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, an edict ordered officials who had not yet taken part to deliberate in detail and report; this was then shelved, and in the end the four men were used.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and an edict called for further deliberation by officials who had not yet spoken; the order was then shelved, and in the end the four were adopted.

sentences.zh: 時楊萬里亦謂張浚當配食，爭之不從，補外。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Wanli also held that Zhang Jun ought to receive joint worship; he argued but was not followed and was sent out to an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wanli also argued that Zhang Jun should receive joint worship; overruled, he was sent to a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 進袤權禮部侍郎兼同修國史侍講，又兼直學士院。

translations.literal: Mao was advanced to Acting Vice Minister of Rites while concurrently Associate Compiler of the National History and Lecturer, and also concurrently Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was promoted to acting vice minister of rites while also associate compiler of the national history and lecturer, and concurrently attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 力辭，上聽免直院。

translations.literal: He pressed to decline; the emperor heard him and exempted him from the Academy post.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed to decline, and the emperor released him from the Academy post.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年，將有事於明堂，詔議升配，袤主紹興孫近、陳公輔之說，謂：「方在几筵，不可配帝，且曆舉郊歲在喪服中者凡四，惟元祐明堂用呂大防請，升配神考，時去大祥止百餘日，且祖宗悉用以日易月之制，故升侑無嫌。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chunxi, when the Hall of Enlightened Rule ceremony was to be held, an edict sought discussion of ascending joint worship; Mao upheld the views of Shaoxing's Sun Jin and Chen Gongfu, saying: "While still at the mourning tablets one cannot worship with the Thearch; moreover, reviewing suburban years spent in mourning dress, there are four in all—only at the Yuanyou Hall of Enlightened Rule, on Lü Dagui's request, was Shenzong elevated in joint worship, when only a little more than a hundred days remained before the end of great mourning, and the ancestors all used the system of substituting days for months, so ascending joint worship raised no objection.
translations.idiomatic: In 1187, as preparations began for the Hall of Enlightened Rule ceremony, the throne called for debate on ascending joint worship; Mao followed Sun Jin and Chen Gongfu of the Shaoxing reign, arguing that while mourning tablets still stood one could not worship alongside the Thearch, that of four suburban years spent in mourning dress only the Yuanyou ceremony, on Lü Dagui's petition, had elevated Shenzong—and then only because a little more than a hundred days remained before great mourning ended and ancestors had all used the practice of substituting days for months.

sentences.zh: 今陛下行三年之喪，高宗雖已祔廟，百官猶未吉服，詎可近違紹興而遠法元祐升侑之禮？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty observes three years' mourning; though Gaozong has already been enshrined, the hundred officials have not yet put on auspicious dress—how can one near violate Shaoxing and far follow Yuanyou's ascending joint worship rite?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty is observing three years' mourning; though Gaozong has been enshrined, officials have not yet donned auspicious dress—how can we set aside recent Shaoxing precedent to follow distant Yuanyou practice?

sentences.zh: 請俟喪畢議之。」

translations.literal: I beg to await the end of mourning before discussing it."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the question be deferred until mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved his view.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘗論人才，袤奏曰：「近召趙汝愚，中外皆喜，如王蘭亦望收召。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong once discussed talent; Mao memorialized: "Recently Zhao Ruyu was summoned—inside and outside the court all rejoiced; Wang Lan too is hoped to be recalled."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong once discussed talent, Mao memorialized that the recent recall of Zhao Ruyu had delighted court and country alike, and that Wang Lan too deserved recall.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it shall be."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So be it."

sentences.zh: 一日論事久，上曰：「如卿才識，近世罕有。」

translations.literal: One day, after a long discussion of affairs, the emperor said: "Talent and insight like yours are rarely seen in recent times."
translations.idiomatic: One day, after a long discussion of affairs, the emperor said, "Talent and insight like yours are rarely seen in recent times."

sentences.zh: 次日語宰執曰：「尤袤甚好，前此無一人言之，何也？」

translations.literal: The next day he told the chief councilors: "You Mao is excellent—before this not a single person spoke of him; why?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the chief councilors, "You Mao is excellent—why has no one spoken of him until now?"

sentences.zh: 兼權中書舍人，復詔兼直學士院，力辭，且薦陸遊自代，上不許。

translations.literal: He was concurrently Acting Palace Secretariat Drafter; again an edict made him concurrently Attendant of the Academy, but he pressed to decline and moreover recommended Lu You to replace him—the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made acting palace secretariat drafter; when again ordered to serve in the Academy he declined and recommended Lu You to replace him, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 時內禪議已定，猶未論大臣也。

translations.literal: At the time the plan for inner abdication was already settled, but the chief ministers had not yet been discussed.
translations.idiomatic: By then the plan for the emperor's abdication was settled, though the chief ministers had not yet been chosen.

sentences.zh: 是日諭袤曰：「旦夕制冊甚多，非卿孰能為者，故處卿以文字之職。」

translations.literal: That day he instructed Mao: "Soon there will be many edicts and ordinances—who but you could draft them? Therefore I place you in a literary post."
translations.idiomatic: That day he told Mao, "Many edicts and ordinances will be needed at once—who but you can draft them? That is why I keep you in a literary post."

sentences.zh: 袤乃拜命，內禪一時制冊，人服其雅正。

translations.literal: Mao then accepted the commission; the edicts and ordinances of the inner abdication at one stroke—people admired their elegant correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Mao accepted the charge, and the abdication documents he drafted at once won admiration for their elegant correctness.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，起知婺州，改太平州，除煥章閣待制，召除給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou, changed to Taiping Prefecture, made Awaiting Draft in the Hall of Glorious Culture, and summoned as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1190 he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou, transferred to Taiping Prefecture, made awaiting draft in the Hall of Glorious Culture, and summoned as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 既就職，即昌言曰：「老矣，無所補報。

translations.literal: Once he took office he spoke forthrightly: "I am old and have nothing left to repay.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he declared openly, "I am old and have little left to offer the throne.

sentences.zh: 凡貴近營求內除小礙法制者，雖特旨令書請，有去而已，必不奉詔。」

translations.literal: Whenever the powerful and intimate sought inner appointments that slightly impeded regulations—even if a special edict ordered drafting the request—I would leave rather than comply, and will certainly not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever powerful favorites sought palace appointments that bent the rules, even under special edict ordering me to draft the request, I would resign rather than obey—and I mean it."

sentences.zh: 甫數日，中貴四人希賞，欲自正使轉橫行，袤繳奏者三，竟格不下。

translations.literal: Within a few days four inner favorites hoped for rewards and wished to transfer from regular commissioner to transverse commissioner; Mao returned the memorial three times, and in the end it was blocked and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Within days four palace favorites sought rewards, asking to advance from regular commissioner to transverse commissioner; Mao returned the draft three times, and it was blocked in the end.

sentences.zh: 兼侍講，入對，言：「願上謹天戒，下畏物情，內正一心，外正五事，澄神寡欲，保毓太和，虛己任賢，酬酢庶務。

translations.literal: Concurrently Lecturer, he entered audience and said: "I wish that Your Majesty above heed Heaven's warnings, below fear the people's feelings, inwardly rectify the one heart, outwardly rectify the five affairs, clarify the spirit and lessen desires, preserve and nurture the Great Harmony, empty the self and employ the worthy, and respond to the myriad tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Also lecturing the heir apparent, he said at audience, "May Your Majesty heed Heaven's warnings above and fear the people's feelings below; rectify your inner heart and outward conduct; clarify the spirit, lessen desires, and preserve the Great Harmony; empty yourself and employ the worthy; and respond to the myriad tasks of state.

sentences.zh: 不在於勞精神、耗思慮、屑屑事為之末也。」

translations.literal: It does not lie in toiling the spirit, exhausting thought, and petty engagement in the least of affairs."
translations.idiomatic: It does not lie in wearing out your spirit and thought on petty busywork."

sentences.zh: 陳源除在京宮觀，耶律適嘿除承宣使，陸安轉遙郡，王成特補官，謝淵、李孝友賞轉官，吳元充、夏永壽遷秩，皆論駁之，上並聽納。

translations.literal: Chen Yuan's appointment to a capital metropolitan temple post, Yelü Shihe's appointment as commissioner-in-ordinary, Lu An's transfer to a distant prefecture, Wang Cheng's special supplemental appointment, Xie Yuan's and Li Xiaoyou's reward promotions, Wu Yuancong's and Xia Yongshou's rank advances—all were debated and rejected by Mao, and the emperor in each case listened and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He debated and rejected appointments for Chen Yuan to a capital sinecure, Yelü Shihe as commissioner-in-ordinary, Lu An's transfer to a distant prefecture, Wang Cheng's special supplemental post, reward promotions for Xie Yuan and Li Xiaoyou, and rank advances for Wu Yuancong and Xia Yongshou—and the emperor accepted his objections in every case.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄以武功大夫、和州防禦使用應辦賞直轉橫行，袤繳奏，謂：「正使有止法，可回授不可直轉。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou, as Martial Achievement Grand Master and Hezhou defense commissioner, used his reward quota from supply duties to transfer to transverse commissioner; Mao returned the memorial, saying: "Regular commissioners have a stopping rule—reassignment is permitted, direct transfer is not.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou, as Martial Achievement Grand Master and defense commissioner of Hezhou, used his supply-duty reward quota to seek promotion to transverse commissioner; Mao returned the draft, saying that regular commissioners had a statutory ceiling—reassignment was permitted, direct promotion was not.

sentences.zh: 侂胄勳賢之後，不宜首壞國法，開攀援之門。」

translations.literal: Tuozhou is descendant of meritorious worthies—it is not fitting that he be first to break state law and open the gate of patronage climbing."
translations.idiomatic: As descendant of meritorious ministers, Tuozhou should not be the first to break state law and open the door to patronage.

sentences.zh: 奏入，手詔令書行，袤復奏：「侂胄四年間已轉二十七年合轉之官，今又欲超授四階，復轉二十年之官，是朝廷官爵專徇侂胄之求，非所以為摩厲之具也。」

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, a hand edict ordered drafting and issuance; Mao again memorialized: "In four years Tuozhou has already been promoted through twenty-seven years' worth of regular promotions; now he again wishes to be granted four ranks beyond rule and promoted through twenty more years' worth of offices—this makes court offices and titles serve Tuozhou's requests alone, not the means to encourage and sharpen men."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, a hand edict ordered it drafted and issued; Mao memorialized again that in four years Tuozhou had already received promotions worth twenty-seven years of regular advancement, and now sought four ranks beyond rule plus twenty more years' worth of offices—that court rank would serve Tuozhou alone, not the means to encourage merit.

sentences.zh: 命遂格。

translations.literal: The order was then blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The order was blocked.

sentences.zh: 上以疾，一再不省重華宮，袤上封事曰：「壽皇事高宗曆二十八年如一日，陛下所親見，今不待倦勤以宗社付陛下，當思所以不負其托，望勿憚一日之勤，以解都人之惑。」

translations.literal: The emperor, on grounds of illness, repeatedly did not visit Chonghua Palace; Mao submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Shouhuang served Gaozong for twenty-eight years as a single day—Your Majesty saw this with your own eyes; now, without waiting for weariness from toil, he entrusted the altars of state and grain to Your Majesty—you should think how not to fail his trust, and I hope you will not shrink from a single day's diligence to dispel the capital people's doubts."
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness, the emperor repeatedly failed to visit Chonghua Palace; Mao submitted a sealed memorial: "Shouhuang served Gaozong for twenty-eight years with unwavering devotion—Your Majesty saw this yourself. He has entrusted the realm to you before growing weary in office; think how not to betray that trust, and do not shrink from even one day's effort to quiet the capital's doubts."

sentences.zh: 後數日，駕即過重華宮。

translations.literal: A few days later the imperial carriage at once passed through Chonghua Palace.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the emperor went to Chonghua Palace.

sentences.zh: 侍御史林大中以論事左遷，袤率左史樓鑰論奏，疏入，不報，皆封駁不書黃。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Lin Dazhong was demoted to the left for discussing affairs; Mao led Left Historiographer Lou Yue in a memorial of discussion; when the memorial entered there was no response—they all sealed and rejected without drafting the yellow edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Attending Censor Lin Dazhong was demoted for remonstrating, Mao led Left Historiographer Lou Yue in a joint memorial; it received no response, and they sealed and rejected subsequent drafts without signing the yellow edict.

sentences.zh: 耶律適嘿復以手除詔承宣使，一再繳奏，輒奉內批，特與書行。

translations.literal: Yelü Shihe again received by hand appointment an edict making him commissioner-in-ordinary; Mao returned the memorial repeatedly, yet each time received an inner endorsement ordering special drafting and issuance.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Shihe again received a hand appointment as commissioner-in-ordinary; Mao returned the draft repeatedly, but each time an inner endorsement ordered it drafted and issued anyway.

sentences.zh: 袤言：「天下者祖宗之天下，爵祿者祖宗之爵祿，壽皇以祖宗之天下傳陛下，安可私用祖宗爵祿而加於公議不允之人哉？」

translations.literal: Mao said: "The realm is the ancestors' realm; offices and stipends are the ancestors' offices and stipends; Shouhuang transmitted the ancestors' realm to Your Majesty—how can one privately use the ancestors' offices and stipends to bestow them on one whom public discussion does not approve?"
translations.idiomatic: Mao said, "The realm belongs to the ancestors, and rank and stipend belong to the ancestors. Shouhuang passed the ancestors' realm to Your Majesty—how can you privately bestow the ancestors' offices and stipends on someone public opinion rejects?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，上震怒，裂去後奏，付前二奏出。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly angered, tore away the later memorial, and ordered the first two memorials issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor flew into a rage, tore up the latest submission, and ordered the first two drafts issued.

sentences.zh: 袤以後奏不報，使吏收閣，命遂不行。

translations.literal: Because the later memorial received no report, Mao had clerks collect and shelve it, and the order was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When the later memorial went unanswered, Mao had clerks collect and shelve it, and the order never took effect.

sentences.zh: 中宮謁家廟，官吏推賞者百七十有二人，袤力言其濫，乞痛裁節，上從之。

translations.literal: When the empress visited the clan temple, officials recommended rewards for one hundred seventy-two persons; Mao strongly said it was excessive and begged severe cutting and restraint; the emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress visited the clan temple, officials recommended rewards for 172 people; Mao protested that the list was excessive and begged sharp cuts, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘗因登對，專論廢法用例之弊，至是復申言之。

translations.literal: He had once, on ascending for audience, devoted discussion to the abuse of abandoning law and using precedent; at this time he again stated it.
translations.idiomatic: He had once devoted an audience to the abuse of setting law aside in favor of precedent; now he raised the point again.

sentences.zh: 除禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 駕當詣重華宮，復以疾不出，率同列奏言：「壽皇有免到宮之命，願力請而往，庶幾可以慰釋群疑，增光孝治。」

translations.literal: When the carriage was to go to Chonghua Palace, again on grounds of illness he did not go out; Mao led his colleagues in memorializing: "Shouhuang has an order exempting attendance at the palace; I wish to press earnestly to go, so that perhaps group doubts may be comforted and released and filial governance may gain luster."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was to visit Chonghua Palace he again pleaded illness and stayed away; Mao led his colleagues in a memorial: "Shouhuang has granted exemption from visiting the palace, but I beg you to press earnestly to go, so that you may ease widespread doubts and lend luster to filial rule."

sentences.zh: 後三日，駕隨出，中外歡呼。

translations.literal: Three days later the carriage followed and went out; inside and outside the court cheered.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the emperor went out after all, and court and country erupted in cheers.

sentences.zh: 兼侍讀，上封事曰：「近年以來，給舍、台諫論事，往往不行，如黃裳、鄭汝諧事遷延一月，如陳源者奉祠，人情固已驚愕，至薑特立召，尤為駭聞。

translations.literal: Concurrently Lecturer, he submitted a sealed memorial saying: "In recent years, when supervising secretaries and censorate remonstrators discuss affairs, their views often are not followed—such as Huang Shang's and Zheng Ruhe's matters delayed a month; such as Chen Yuan receiving a temple appointment—popular feeling was already startled and alarmed; as for Jiang Teli's summons, it is especially shocking to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Also lecturing the heir apparent, he submitted a sealed memorial: "In recent years remonstrances from supervising secretaries and censors have often been ignored—Huang Shang's and Zheng Ruhe's cases dragged on for a month; Chen Yuan was given a temple appointment, which already shocked opinion; but the recall of Jiang Teli is especially alarming.

sentences.zh: 向特立得志之時，昌言台諫皆其門人，竊弄威福，一旦斥去，莫不誦陛下英斷。

translations.literal: When Teli formerly had his way, he openly said that censorate remonstrators were all his disciples and secretly wielded authority and favor; once he was driven out, none failed to praise Your Majesty's heroic decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: When Teli was in power he boasted that censors were all his disciples and secretly wielded authority; when you drove him out, everyone praised your decisive judgment.

sentences.zh: 今遽召之，自古去小人甚難，譬除蔓草，猶且復生，況加封植乎？

translations.literal: Now to summon him hastily—from antiquity removing petty men has been very difficult; it is like clearing creeping weeds, which still grow back—how much more if one adds planting and cultivation?
translations.idiomatic: To recall him now is perilous: removing petty men has always been hard, like clearing weeds that grow back—how much worse if you cultivate them again?

sentences.zh: 若以源、特立有勞，優以外任，或加錫齎，無所不可。

translations.literal: If because Yuan and Teli have merit one favors them with outside appointment, or adds gifts and bounty, nothing is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: If Yuan and Teli have earned favor, reward them with outside posts or gifts—anything but recall to court.

sentences.zh: 彼其閑廢已久，含憤蓄怨，待此而發，儻復呼之，必將潛引黨類，力排異己，朝廷無由安靜。」

translations.literal: They have long been idle and dismissed, harboring resentment and storing grievance, waiting for this to erupt; if they are again summoned, they will surely secretly draw in factional associates and forcefully exclude those unlike themselves—the court will have no means to be tranquil."
translations.idiomatic: They have long brooded in disgrace, nursing grievances for this moment; if you call them back they will surely recruit factions and drive out rivals, and the court will never know peace."

sentences.zh: 時上已屬疾，國事多舛，袤積憂成疾，請告，不報。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor already entrusted his illness; state affairs were mostly awry; Mao's accumulated worry became illness; he requested leave, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already seriously ill and state affairs were in disarray; Mao's worries turned to illness; he requested leave but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 疾篤乞致仕，又不服，遂卒，年七十。

translations.literal: When his illness was grave he begged to retire; again it was not granted; he then died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave he begged to retire, was again refused, and died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 遺奏大略勸上以孝事兩宮，以勤康庶政，察邪佞，護善類。

translations.literal: His final memorial in outline urged the emperor to serve the two palaces with filial piety, to labor diligently in governing the myriad affairs, to discern the wicked and flatterers, and to protect good men.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial urged the emperor to serve both palaces filially, work diligently at governance, discern the wicked, and protect good men.

sentences.zh: 又口占遺書別政府。

translations.literal: He also orally composed a final letter to take leave of the Council.
translations.idiomatic: He also dictated a farewell letter to the Council.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉正奉大夫致仕。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Grand Master of Court and retired.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was posthumously granted retirement as Grand Master of Court.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 袤少從喻樗、汪應辰遊。

translations.literal: Mao in youth followed Yu Chu and Wang Yingchen in study.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Mao studied under Yu Chu and Wang Yingchen.

sentences.zh: 樗學于楊時，時，程頤高弟也。

translations.literal: Chu studied under Yang Shi; Shi was a leading disciple of Cheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Chu had studied under Yang Shi, a leading disciple of Cheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 方乾道、淳熙間，程氏學稍振，忌之者目為道學，將攻之。

translations.literal: Around the Qiandao and Chunxi reigns, Cheng learning slightly revived; those who envied it labeled it "Daoxue" and were about to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiandao and Chunxi reigns Cheng learning revived somewhat; envious critics labeled it "Daoxue" and prepared to attack it.

sentences.zh: 袤在掖垣，首言：「夫道學者，堯、舜所以帝，禹、湯、武所以王，周公、孔、孟所以設教。

translations.literal: Mao, in the palace secretariat, was first to say: "As for Daoxue—it is what made Yao and Shun emperors, what made Yu, Tang, and Wu kings, what made the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius establish teaching.
translations.idiomatic: While in the palace secretariat Mao was the first to say: "Daoxue is what made Yao and Shun emperors, Yu, Tang, and Wu kings, and the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius teachers of the realm.

sentences.zh: 近立此名，詆訾士君子，故臨財不苟得所謂廉介，安貧守分所謂恬退，擇言顧行所謂踐履，行己有恥所謂名節，皆目之為道學。

translations.literal: Recently this name was established to slander scholar-gentlemen—thus not grasping gain when facing wealth, called integrity; peacefully accepting poverty and keeping one's place, called quiet withdrawal; choosing words and looking to conduct, called practice; having shame in one's conduct, called name and integrity—all are labeled Daoxue.
translations.idiomatic: Recently this label has been used to slander gentlemen—integrity in refusing ill-gotten wealth, quiet withdrawal in accepting poverty, careful speech and conduct, shame in one's own behavior—all are called Daoxue.

sentences.zh: 此名一立，賢人君子欲自見於世，一舉足且入其中，俱無得免，此豈盛世所宜有？

translations.literal: Once this name is established, worthy men and gentlemen who wish to show themselves in the world—with a single step enter into it and none can escape; is this what a flourishing age should have?
translations.idiomatic: Once this label exists, any worthy man who steps forward falls under suspicion—can a flourishing age afford that?

sentences.zh: 願徇名必責其實，聽言必觀其行，人才庶不壞於疑似。」

translations.literal: I wish that in following names one must demand their reality, and in hearing words one must observe conduct—then talent may not be ruined in seeming resemblance."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that names be tested by deeds and words by conduct, so talent is not destroyed by mere suspicion."

sentences.zh: 孝宗曰：「道學豈不美之名，正恐假託為奸，使真偽相亂爾。

translations.literal: Xiaozong said: "Is not Daoxue a fine name? I precisely fear that people falsely borrow it for treachery and make true and false mutually confused.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong said, "Daoxue is a fine name—but I fear men will borrow it for treachery and blur truth and falsehood.

sentences.zh: 待付出戒敕之。」

translations.literal: Wait until it is issued and send out a prohibitory edict."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a prohibitory edict drafted."

sentences.zh: 袤死數年，侂胄擅國，於是禁錮道學，賢士大夫皆受其禍，識者以袤為知言。

translations.literal: Several years after Mao's death, Tuozhou monopolized the state; thereupon Daoxue was proscribed and imprisoned, and worthy scholar-officials all suffered disaster—those with insight took Mao as one who spoke with foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Years after Mao's death Tuozhou seized power, proscribed Daoxue, and worthy officials suffered—those with insight judged Mao prescient.

sentences.zh: 嘗取孫綽《遂初賦》以自號，光宗書扁賜之。

translations.literal: He once took Sun Chuo's "Rhapsody on First Retirement" as his style name; Guangzong wrote a plaque and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself after Sun Chuo's "Rhapsody on First Retirement," and Guangzong wrote a plaque and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 有《遂初小稿》六十卷、《內外制》三十卷。

translations.literal: He had "Drafts of First Retirement" in sixty juan and "Inner and Outer Edicts" in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Drafts of First Retirement in sixty juan and Inner and Outer Edicts in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 嘉定五年，諡文簡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiading he was given the posthumous title Wénjiǎn.
translations.idiomatic: In 1212 he received the posthumous title Wénjiǎn (Cultivated and Simple).

sentences.zh: 子棐、概。

translations.literal: His sons were Fei and Gai.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Fei and Gai.

sentences.zh: 孫焴，禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandson Yu was Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yu became minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 謝諤，字昌國，臨江軍新喻人。

translations.literal: Xie E, courtesy name Changguo, was a native of Xinyu in Linjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Xie E, whose courtesy name was Changguo, came from Xinyu in Linjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 幼敏惠，日記千言，為文立成。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and clever; he memorized a thousand words daily and composed essays on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick and clever, memorized a thousand characters a day, and could compose essays at once.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十七年，中進士第，調峽州夷陵縣主簿，未上，撫之樂安多盜，監司檄諤攝尉，條二十策，大要使其徒相糾而以信賞隨之，群盜果解散。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as chief clerk of Yiling County in Xia Prefecture, and had not yet reported when Le'an in Fu Circuit had many bandits; the supervisory office ordered E to act as sheriff; he set forth twenty measures, the main point being to make the bandits inform on one another and follow with trusted rewards and punishments—the bandit groups truly dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1157 he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as chief clerk of Yiling in Xia Prefecture; before reporting he was ordered to act as sheriff in Le'an, Fu Circuit, where bandits were numerous. He drafted twenty measures, chiefly to set bandits informing on one another with reliable rewards and punishments, and the gangs dispersed.

sentences.zh: 金渝盟，諸軍往來境上，選行縣事，有治辦聲。

translations.literal: When the Jin violated the treaty, armies came and went on the border; he was selected to handle county affairs and had a reputation for effective governance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin broke the treaty and armies crossed the border, he was chosen to handle county affairs and earned a reputation for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 改吉州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Judicial Administrator of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to judicial administrator of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 囚死者舊瘞以鞂，往往暴骨。

translations.literal: Dead prisoners were formerly buried with matting and often had their bones exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Dead prisoners had been buried in matting, and their bones were often left exposed.

sentences.zh: 諤白郡，取船官棄材以棺斂之。

translations.literal: E informed the prefecture, took discarded timber from the shipping office, and used coffins to bury them properly.
translations.idiomatic: E reported to the prefecture, took discarded timber from the shipping office, and gave the dead proper coffin burial.

sentences.zh: 郡民陳氏僮竊其篋以逃，有匿之者。

translations.literal: A Chen family servant in the prefecture stole their strongbox and fled; someone hid him.
translations.idiomatic: A servant of the Chen family stole their strongbox and fled, and someone hid him.

sentences.zh: 陳于官，詞過其實，反為匿僮者所誣。

translations.literal: Chen reported to the authorities; his words exceeded the facts, and he was in turn slandered by the one who hid the servant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen reported to the authorities, but his account exaggerated the facts, and the man who hid the servant turned the charge back on him.

sentences.zh: 帥龔茂良怒，欲坐以罪，諤為書白茂良，陳氏獲免，茂良亦以是知之。

translations.literal: Commander Gong Maoliang was angry and wished to convict him; E wrote a letter explaining to Maoliang, and the Chen family was spared; Maoliang also came to know him through this.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Gong Maoliang was furious and meant to punish Chen; E wrote to explain, Chen was spared, and Maoliang came to know E's worth.

sentences.zh: 歲大侵，饑民萬余求廩，官吏罔措。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine, more than ten thousand starving people sought grain from the granary; officials were at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe famine more than ten thousand starving people sought grain while officials stood helpless.

sentences.zh: 諤植五色旗，分部給糶，頃刻而定。

translations.literal: E planted five-colored flags, divided areas and issued relief grain sales, and in a moment it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: E raised five-colored flags, divided districts, and issued relief grain; order was restored in moments.

sentences.zh: 知袁州分宜縣。

translations.literal: He governed Fenyi County in Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Fenyi in Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 縣積負於郡數十萬，歲常賦外，又征緡錢二萬餘，諤乃疏其弊于諸監司，請免之。

translations.literal: The county had accumulated debts to the prefecture of several hundred thousand; beyond the annual regular levy, more than twenty thousand in cash was also collected; E then memorialized the abuses to the supervisory offices and requested exemption.
translations.idiomatic: The county owed the prefecture hundreds of thousands in accumulated debt and paid more than twenty thousand cash beyond the annual levy; E reported the abuses to supervisory officials and sought exemption.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父憂，服闋，除幹辦行在諸司糧料院。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his father; when mourning ended he was appointed Administrator in the Capital Commissariat for Various Offices Grain and Forage.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he mourned his father; when mourning ended he was appointed administrator in the Capital Commissariat for grain and forage.

sentences.zh: 遷國子監簿，尋擢監察御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Registrar of the Directorate of Education and soon promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became registrar of the Directorate of Education and soon investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 奏減袁州分宜、秀州華亭月樁錢。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce the monthly assessment money of Fenyi in Yuan Prefecture and Huating in Xiu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to reduce the monthly assessment levies on Fenyi in Yuan Prefecture and Huating in Xiu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諤裏居時，創義役法，編為一書，至是上之。

translations.literal: While living in his home district, E created the voluntary labor service law and compiled it into a book; at this time he submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: While living at home he devised a voluntary labor-service law and compiled it into a book, which he now submitted.

sentences.zh: 詔行其法于諸路，民以為便。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his law implemented through the circuits; the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered it implemented in all circuits, to the people's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，再遷右諫議大夫兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor, then again to Right Remonstrator while concurrently Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He became attending censor, then right remonstrator while also lecturing the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 講《尚書》，言於上曰：「《書》，治道之本，故觀經者當以《書》為本。」

translations.literal: Lecturing on the Documents, he said to the emperor: "The Documents are the root of the way of governance; therefore one who views the classics should take the Documents as root."
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing on the Documents, he told the emperor, "The Documents are the root of governance; anyone studying the classics should begin there."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕最喜伊尹、傅說所學，得事君之道。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I most delight in what Yi Yin and Fu Yue studied—I obtain the way of serving the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I delight most in what Yi Yin and Fu Yue taught—the way of serving one's ruler."

sentences.zh: 諤曰：「伊、傅固然，非成湯、武丁信用之，亦安能致治！」

translations.literal: E said: "Yi and Fu are certainly so—but without Cheng Tang and Wu Ding trusting and employing them, how could they have brought about good governance!"
translations.idiomatic: E replied, "Yi and Fu are surely admirable—but without Cheng Tang and Wu Ding trusting and employing them, how could they have brought order?"

sentences.zh: 因論及邊事，上有乘機會之諭，諤曰：「機會雖不可失，舉事亦不可輕。」

translations.literal: Thereupon they discussed border affairs; the emperor had words about seizing opportunity; E said: "Opportunity though it may not be lost, undertaking affairs also may not be light."
translations.idiomatic: They turned to border affairs; when the emperor spoke of seizing opportunity, E said, "Opportunity must not be missed, but action must not be rash either."

sentences.zh: 上嘗問曰：「聞卿與郭雍遊，雍學問甚好，豈曾見程頤乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked: "I hear you associated with Guo Yong—Yong's learning is very good; did he ever see Cheng Yi?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked, "I hear you studied with Guo Yong, whose learning is excellent—did he ever meet Cheng Yi?"

sentences.zh: 諤奏：「雍父忠孝嘗事頤，雍蓋得其傳于父。」

translations.literal: E memorialized: "Yong's father Zhongxiao once served Yi; Yong probably obtained the transmission from his father."
translations.idiomatic: E answered, "Yong's father Zhongxiao once studied under Yi; Yong inherited the tradition from his father."

sentences.zh: 上遂封雍為頤正先生。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon enfeoffed Yong as Master Yizheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ennobled Yong as Master Yizheng.

sentences.zh: 光宗登極，獻十箴，又論二節三近：所當節者曰宴飲，曰妄費；

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended the throne, he presented ten admonitions and also discussed two things to restrain and three things to draw near: what should be restrained were feasting and drinking and reckless spending;
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended the throne he presented ten admonitions and discussed two restraints and three closenesses: restrain feasting and reckless spending;

sentences.zh: 所當近者曰執政大臣，曰舊學名儒，曰經筵列職。

translations.literal: what should be drawn near were chief administering ministers, renowned old scholars, and lecturers at the classics mat.
translations.idiomatic: draw near chief ministers, renowned old scholars, and lecturers at the classics mat.

sentences.zh: 除御史中丞，權工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censor-in-Chief and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed censor-in-chief and acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 請祠，以煥章閣直學士知泉州，又辭，提舉太平興國宮而歸。

translations.literal: He requested a shrine appointment, was made Academician of the Hall of Glorious Culture and prefect of Quanzhou, declined again, and returned after being made intendant of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a sinecure, was made academician of the Hall of Glorious Culture and prefect of Quanzhou, declined again, and returned as intendant of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年，卒，年七十四，贈通議大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxi he died, aged seventy-four, and was posthumously given Master of Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1194 at seventy-four and was posthumously ennobled as Master of Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 諤為文仿歐陽修、曾鞏。

translations.literal: E's writing imitated Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His prose imitated Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong.

sentences.zh: 初居縣南之竹坡，名其燕坐曰艮齋，人稱艮齋先生。

translations.literal: At first he lived at Bamboo Slope south of the county, named his seated repose the Gen Studio, and people called him Master Gen Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He first lived at Bamboo Slope south of the county, named his study the Gen Studio, and was known as Master Gen Studio.

sentences.zh: 周必大薦士，及諤姓名，孝宗曰：「是謂艮齋者耶？

translations.literal: Zhou Bida recommended scholars; when E's name came up, Xiaozong said: "Is this the one called Master Gen Studio?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Bida recommended scholars and E's name appeared, Xiaozong said, "Is this the man they call Master Gen Studio?

sentences.zh: 朕見其《性學淵源》五卷而得之」云。

translations.literal: I saw his five juan Origins of the Learning of Nature and obtained understanding of him," he said."
translations.idiomatic: I learned of him from his five-juan Origins of the Learning of Nature," he said."

sentences.zh: 顏師魯

translations.literal: Yan Shilu
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shilu

sentences.zh: 顏師魯，字幾聖，漳州龍溪人。

translations.literal: Yan Shilu, courtesy name Jisheng, was a native of Longxi in Zhang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shilu, whose courtesy name was Jisheng, came from Longxi in Zhang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，擢進士第，曆知莆田、福清縣。

translations.literal: During Shaoxing he was selected in the jinshi degree and successively governed Putian and Fuqing counties.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing reign he passed the jinshi examination and served successively as magistrate of Putian and Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 嘗決水利滯訟，辟陂洫綿四十里。

translations.literal: He once resolved stalled lawsuits over water conservancy and opened irrigation extending forty li.
translations.idiomatic: He once cleared backlog in water-rights lawsuits and opened irrigation works stretching forty li.

sentences.zh: 歲大侵，發廩勸分有方而不遏糴價，船粟畢湊，市糴更平。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine he opened granaries and encouraged sharing with method but did not suppress grain-sale prices; boat grain all gathered, and market grain purchases became more level.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he opened granaries and encouraged sharing without suppressing grain prices; grain boats converged and market prices stabilized.

sentences.zh: 鄭伯熊為常平使，薦于朝，帥陳俊卿尤器重之。

translations.literal: Zheng Boxiong as Ever-Normal intendant recommended him to court; Commander Chen Junqing especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Boxiong, as Ever-Normal intendant, recommended him to court, and Commander Chen Junqing especially valued him.

sentences.zh: 召為官告院，遷國子丞，除江東提舉。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Office of Official Announcements, transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and appointed Jiangdong intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Office of Official Announcements, became vice director of the Directorate of Education, and was appointed Jiangdong intendant.

sentences.zh: 時天雨土，日青無光，都人相驚，師魯陛辭，言：「田裏未安，犴獄未清，政令未當，忠邪未辨，天不示變，人主何繇省悟！

translations.literal: At the time earth rained from heaven, the sun was blue-green without light, and capital people were mutually alarmed; Shilu, on audience for farewell, said: "Fields and hamlets are not at peace, prisons are not cleared, government orders are not correct, loyal and wicked are not distinguished—if Heaven does not display transformations, by what means can the sovereign awaken to reflection!
translations.idiomatic: When earth rained from the sky, the sun turned dim and greenish, and the capital panicked, Shilu took leave of audience and said, "The countryside is unsettled, prisons uncleared, policies awry, loyal and wicked undistinguished—if Heaven shows no sign, how can the ruler awaken?

sentences.zh: 願詔中外，極陳得失，求所以答天戒，銷患未形。」

translations.literal: I wish that an edict order inside and outside the court to state gains and losses to the utmost, seeking the means to answer Heaven's warning and dissolve calamity before it takes form."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty order court and provinces to state gains and losses fully, answer Heaven's warning, and dissolve disaster before it forms."

sentences.zh: 上韙其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 尋改使浙西。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to commissioner for Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to commissioner for Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 役法敝甚，細民至以雞豚罌榻折產力，遇役輒破家。

translations.literal: The labor service law was very decayed; petty people even used chickens, pigs, jars, and bedding to break their productive power—when corvée came they promptly ruined their families.
translations.idiomatic: The labor-service law had decayed so badly that commoners sold chickens, pigs, and household goods to meet levies and were ruined whenever corvée fell due.

sentences.zh: 師魯下教屬邑，預正流水籍，稽其役之序，寬比限，免代輸，咸便安之。

translations.literal: Shilu issued instructions to subordinate counties, beforehand rectified flowing-water registers, examined the order of their labor, broadened comparison limits, exempted substitute payments—all found it convenient and were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu ordered subordinate counties to rectify household registers, set the order of service, broaden deadlines, and exempt substitute payments, to everyone's relief.

sentences.zh: 鹽課歲百钜萬，本錢久不給，亭灶私鬻，禁不可止，刑辟日繁。

translations.literal: Salt revenue yearly reached millions; principal capital long went unpaid; salterns privately sold, prohibition could not be stopped, and penal statutes daily multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Salt revenue ran to millions yearly, but capital went unpaid for years; salterns sold privately despite prohibition, and penal cases multiplied daily.

sentences.zh: 師魯撙帑緡，盡償宿負，戒官吏毋侵移，比旁路課獨最。

translations.literal: Shilu economized treasury cash, fully repaid old debts, warned officials not to divert funds, and compared with neighboring circuits his revenue alone was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu economized treasury funds, repaid all old debts, forbade officials from diverting revenue, and alone among neighboring circuits met his salt quota fully.

sentences.zh: 上謂執政曰：「儒生能辦事如此。」

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief administrators: "A Confucian scholar can handle affairs like this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief ministers, "A Confucian scholar can administer like this."

sentences.zh: 予職直秘閣。

translations.literal: He was given the post Attendant in the Privy Archives.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant in the Privy Archives.

sentences.zh: 農民有墾曠土成田未及受租者，奸豪多為己利，師魯奏：「但當正其租賦，不應繩以盜種法，失劭農重本意。」

translations.literal: When farmers reclaimed wasteland into fields but had not yet received rent assessment, powerful scoundrels often took it for their own profit; Shilu memorialized: "One should only rectify their rent and tax; one should not bind them with the law on illicit cultivation—this loses the heavy original intent of encouraging agriculture."
translations.idiomatic: When farmers reclaimed wasteland before rent was assessed, powerful families often seized the benefit; Shilu memorialized that rent should simply be assessed properly rather than punishing them under laws on illicit cultivation, which betrayed the policy of encouraging farming.

sentences.zh: 奏可，遂著為令。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved and was then written into regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved and written into law.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史，遇事盡言，無所阿撓。

translations.literal: He entered court as Investigating Censor; encountering affairs he spoke fully, with nothing of fawning or bending.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as investigating censor and spoke his mind on every issue without flinching.

sentences.zh: 有自外府得內殿宣引，且將補御史闕員，師魯亟奏：「宋璟召自廣州，道中不與楊思勖交一談。

translations.literal: Someone from an outside prefecture received inner-hall audience introduction and was about to fill a censor vacancy; Shilu urgently memorialized: "Song Jing was summoned from Guangzhou and on the road did not exchange a single conversation with Yang Sixu.
translations.idiomatic: When a man from an outside prefecture received inner-hall audience and was about to fill a censor vacancy, Shilu urgently memorialized: "Song Jing was summoned from Guangzhou and would not speak a word with Yang Sixu on the road.

sentences.zh: 李鄘恥為吐突承璀所薦，堅辭相位不拜。

translations.literal: Li Yong was ashamed to be recommended by Tuoba Chengkan and firmly declined the chief councilor post without accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong was ashamed to be recommended by Tuoba Chengkan and firmly refused the chief councilorship.

sentences.zh: 士大夫未論其才，立身之節，當以璟、鄘為法。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials, before discussing their talent, in the integrity of establishing the person, should take Jing and Yong as models.
translations.idiomatic: Before judging talent, gentlemen should take Jing and Yong as models of personal integrity.

sentences.zh: 今其人朋邪為跡，人所切齒，縱朝廷乏才，寧少此輩乎？

translations.literal: Now this man's factional wickedness is his track, what people gnash teeth over—though the court lacks talent, would it be better to lack this sort?
translations.idiomatic: This man's factional wickedness is notorious; even if the court lacks talent, can we afford men like him?

sentences.zh: 臣雖不肖，羞與為伍。」

translations.literal: Your servant, though unworthy, is ashamed to be of their company."
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I would be ashamed to keep his company."

sentences.zh: 命乃寢。

translations.literal: The order was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was then withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 繼累章論除職帥藩者：「比年好進之徒，平時交結權幸，一紆郡紱，皆掊克以厚包苴，故昔以才稱，後以貪敗。」

translations.literal: He followed with successive memorials on removing officials who held posts while commanding border prefectures: "In recent years careerists, in ordinary times forming ties with powerful favorites, once they don the prefect's sash all squeeze and exploit to fatten wrapped bribes; thus those once praised for talent later fell to greed and ruin."
translations.idiomatic: He followed with repeated memorials urging the removal of officials who combined civil posts with command of military districts: "In recent years office-seekers cultivate ties with powerful favorites; once they take up a prefectural post, they squeeze the people to fill their purses with bribes. Men once praised for talent end in disgrace for greed.

sentences.zh: 上出其疏袖中，行之。

translations.literal: The emperor took his memorial from his sleeve and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor produced the memorial from his sleeve and put it into effect.

sentences.zh: 十年，繇太府少卿為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he moved from Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Treasury to Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the reign he was transferred from vice minister of the Court of Imperial Treasury to director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 初，上諭執政擇老成端重者表率太學，故有是命。

translations.literal: At first the emperor instructed the chief ministers to choose men of mature years, steadiness, and weight to set the example at the Imperial University; hence this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had told the chief ministers to choose a mature, dignified man to lead the Imperial University by example, and this appointment followed.

sentences.zh: 首奏：「宜講明理學，嚴禁穿鑿，俾廉恥興而風俗厚。」

translations.literal: In his first memorial he said: "Principle-learning should be expounded clearly, forced textual contrivance strictly forbidden, so that integrity and shame rise and custom grows thick."
translations.idiomatic: In his first memorial he said, "The classics of principle should be taught clearly and forced, far-fetched interpretations forbidden, so that integrity flourishes and public morals are strengthened.

sentences.zh: 師魯學行素孚規約，率以身先，與諸生言，孳孳以治己立誠為本，藝尤異者必加獎勸，由是人知飭勵。

translations.literal: Shilu's learning and conduct had long matched the regulations; he always led by personal example. Speaking with the students, he tirelessly took self-discipline and establishing sincerity as root; those whose arts were especially outstanding he always added encouragement to, and thereby people knew restraint and striving.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu had long lived up to the academy's standards and led by example. He urged students tirelessly to cultivate themselves and keep faith, rewarded exceptional talent, and soon the whole school knew discipline.

sentences.zh: 上聞之喜曰：「顏師魯到學未久，規矩甚肅。」

translations.literal: The emperor heard and said with pleasure: "Yan Shilu has not been long at the academy, yet its rules and measures are very strict."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he said with pleasure, "Yan Shilu has not been at the academy long, yet discipline there is already very strict.

sentences.zh: 除禮部侍郎，尋兼吏部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, and soon additionally held the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of rites and soon also served in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 有旨改官班，特免引見。

translations.literal: An edict changed his rank sequence, and he was specially exempted from presentation at audience.
translations.idiomatic: An edict altered his rank sequence and specially exempted him from the customary audience presentation.

sentences.zh: 師魯獻規曰：「祖宗法度不可輕馳，願始終持久，自強不息。」

translations.literal: Shilu offered admonition, saying: "The ancestral laws and institutions must not be lightly cast aside; I wish that from beginning to end they endure, with unceasing self-strengthening."
translations.idiomatic: Shilu offered counsel: "The laws and institutions of our ancestors must not be lightly abandoned. I pray Your Majesty will uphold them to the end and never cease to strengthen yourself.

sentences.zh: 因言：「賜帶多濫，應奉微勞，皆得橫金預外朝廷會，如觀瞻何？

translations.literal: He then said: "Bestowal of official sashes is much abused; men with trifling service on imperial commissions all get to wear gold and take part in outer-court assemblies—what of public regard?
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Imperial sashes are handed out too freely. Men who perform minor service on imperial errands all wear gold insignia and join outer-court assemblies—what does this do to the court's dignity?

sentences.zh: 且臣下非時之賜，過於優隆；

translations.literal: Moreover, untimely gifts to subordinates exceed what is proper in favor and elevation;
translations.idiomatic: Untimely gifts to officials are already far too generous;

sentences.zh: 梵舍不急之役，亦加錫齎。

translations.literal: Buddhist monasteries' non-urgent projects also receive added imperial grants.
translations.idiomatic: even non-urgent work at Buddhist monasteries receives imperial grants.

sentences.zh: 雖南帑封樁不與大農經費，然無功勞而概與之，是棄之也。

translations.literal: Although the southern treasury's sealed stores do not come from the Minister of Revenue's regular funds, to give them indiscriminately without merit or labor is to throw them away.
translations.idiomatic: Though the southern sealed treasury is separate from the Ministry of Revenue's budget, to hand out its funds without regard to merit is simply to waste them.

sentences.zh: 萬一有為國制變禦侮，建功立事者，將何以旌寵之？」

translations.literal: If by any chance there should be one who for the state's sake reforms institutions, repels insult, and establishes achievement and deeds, by what means will he be honored and rewarded?"
