translations.idiomatic: If someday a man truly reforms the state, repels the enemy, and wins lasting achievement, how will Your Majesty reward him?

sentences.zh: 高宗喪制，一時典禮多師魯裁定，又與禮官尤袤、鄭僑上議廟號，語在《袤傳》。

translations.literal: For Gaozong's mourning rites, many ceremonies of the time were largely settled by Shilu; he also with ritual officials You Mao and Zheng Qiao submitted on the temple name—the account is in the Biography of Mao.
translations.idiomatic: During the mourning rites for Gaozong, Shilu decided most of the ceremonial arrangements. He also joined ritual officials You Mao and Zheng Qiao in memorializing on the temple name; that account appears in You Mao's biography.

sentences.zh: 詔充遺留禮信使。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as leftover tribute and routine mission emissary.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as emissary on the annual leftover-tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 初，顯仁遺留使至金，必令簪花聽樂。

translations.literal: At first, when Xianren's leftover mission emissaries reached Jin, they were always made to wear flowers and listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when emissaries of the leftover-tribute mission for Empress Xianren reached Jin territory, the Jurchens always required them to wear flowers in their hair and listen to music.

sentences.zh: 師魯陛辭，言：「國勢今非昔比，金人或強臣非禮，誓以死守。」

translations.literal: Shilu, on farewell audience, said: "The state's power today is not as of old; should Jin men or powerful ministers treat me without propriety, I swear to defend unto death."
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave of the throne, Shilu said, "Our national strength is not what it once was. If the Jurchens or their powerful ministers treat me discourteously, I swear I will die rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 沿途宴設，力請徹樂。

translations.literal: At banquets set out along the route he forcefully requested that music be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet along the route he firmly asked that the music be stopped.

sentences.zh: 至燕山，復辭簪花執射。

translations.literal: Reaching Yan Mountain, he again declined wearing flowers and performing archery.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan Mountain he again refused to wear flowers or take part in the archery display.

sentences.zh: 時孝宗以孝聞，師魯據經陳誼，反復慷慨，故金終不能奪。

translations.literal: At the time Xiaozong was famed for filial piety; Shilu cited the classics and stated righteous principle, repeatedly and with passion, so Jin in the end could not override him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was then renowned for filial piety. Shilu appealed to the classics with repeated, passionate argument, and in the end the Jurchens could not force him.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，尋除吏部尚書兼侍講，屢抗章請老，以龍圖閣直學士知泉州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, then appointed Minister of Personnel with concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting; repeatedly submitting memorials resisting and requesting retirement, he was made Dragon Hall Attendant Academician and prefect of Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of personnel, then minister of personnel and lecturer-in-waiting. After repeated requests to retire, he was made Dragon Hall attendant academician and prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 台諫、侍從相繼拜疏，引唐孔戣事以留行。

translations.literal: Censors, remonstrators, and attendants-in-waiting successively submitted memorials, citing the Tang case of Kong Kui to ask him to remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: Censors, remonstrators, and attendants-in-waiting submitted memorial after memorial, citing the Tang official Kong Kui's case in asking him to stay at court.

sentences.zh: 內引，奏言：「願親賢積學，以崇聖德，節情制欲，以養清躬。」

translations.literal: At a private audience he memorialized: "I wish that you draw near the worthy and accumulate learning to exalt sagely virtue, restrain emotion and control desire to nourish a pure person."
translations.idiomatic: At a private audience he said, "I pray Your Majesty will keep company with the worthy, continue learning, and thereby exalt your sage virtue; restrain passion and desire, and thereby preserve your pure self.

sentences.zh: 在泉因任，凡閱三年，專以恤民寬屬邑為政，始至即蠲舶貨，諸商賈胡尤服其清。

translations.literal: At Quan he served out his term, in all three years, making policy solely of cherishing the people and easing subordinate districts; upon first arrival he immediately remitted maritime-trade levies, and all merchant traders and foreigners especially submitted to his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He served out a full three-year term at Quanzhou, governing with a single aim of easing the people's burdens and loosening control over subordinate districts. As soon as he arrived he remitted maritime trade levies, and merchants and foreign traders especially respected his integrity.

sentences.zh: 再起知泉州，以紹熙四年卒於家，年七十五。

translations.literal: Recalled again as prefect of Quan, he died at home in the fourth year of Shaoxi, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled again to govern Quanzhou, he died at home in the fourth year of Shaoxi at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 師魯自幼莊重若成人，孝友天至。

translations.literal: From youth Shilu was solemn and grave like an adult; filial piety and brotherly affection were innate to him.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Shilu was as grave as a grown man, and filial devotion came to him by nature.

sentences.zh: 初為番禺簿，喪父以歸，扶柩航海，水程數千里，甫三日登於岸，而颶風大作，人以為孝感。

translations.literal: When he first served as registrar of Panyu, his father died and he returned home, supporting the coffin by sea over a water route of several thousand li; he had just reached shore on the third day when a great hurricane arose, and people took it as filial response moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When he first served as registrar of Panyu, his father died and he sailed home with the coffin over thousands of li of open water. He had been ashore only three days when a great hurricane struck, and people called it Heaven's response to filial piety.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「窮達自有定分，枉道希世，徒喪所守。」

translations.literal: He often said: "Failure and success each have their allotted portion; to bend the Way and court the age only vainly loses what one holds to."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Success and failure have their allotted measure. To bend principle and court the world only throws away what one stands for.

sentences.zh: 故其大節確如金石，雖動與俗情不合，而終翕然信服。

translations.literal: Therefore his great integrity was firm as metal and stone; though his actions often did not accord with common feeling, in the end all submitted and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: His great integrity was as firm as metal and stone. Though his conduct often ran against popular sentiment, in the end everyone submitted to him in trust.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年，詔特賜諡曰定肅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiatai, an edict specially bestowed the posthumous title Ding Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiatai an edict specially granted him the posthumous title Ding Su, "Settled and Stern."

sentences.zh: 袁樞，字機仲，建之建安人。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu, courtesy name Jizhong, was a native of Jian'an in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, whose courtesy name was Jizhong, came from Jian'an in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼力學，嘗以《修身為弓賦》試國子監，周必大、劉珙皆期以遠器。

translations.literal: In youth he applied himself to learning; once with his rhapsody "Self-Cultivation as a Bow" he tested at the Imperial University, and Zhou Bida and Liu Hong both looked to him as far-reaching talent.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied hard. When he submitted his rhapsody "Self-Cultivation as a Bow" at the Imperial University, Zhou Bida and Liu Hong both marked him as a man of far-reaching promise.

sentences.zh: 試禮部，詞賦第一人，調溫州判官，教授興化軍。

translations.literal: Testing at the Ministry of Rites, he took first place in rhapsody and fu; he was assigned as judicial intendant of Wen Prefecture and instructor at Xinghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ministry of Rites examination he ranked first in rhapsody and fu, was assigned as judicial intendant of Wenzhou, and served as instructor at Xinghua Army.

sentences.zh: 乾道七年，為禮部試官，就除太學錄，輪對三疏，一論開言路以養忠孝之氣，二論規恢復當圖萬全，三論士大夫多虛誕、僥榮利。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qiandao he served as examiner for the Ministry of Rites, and upon completion was appointed Recorder of the Imperial University; in rotation audience he submitted three memorials—one on opening the path of speech to nourish the spirit of loyalty and filial piety, one on planning recovery and needing to seek complete security, one on scholar-officials being much given to empty pretense and grasping at glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Qiandao he served as examiner for the Ministry of Rites and was then appointed recorder of the Imperial University. In rotation audience he submitted three memorials: one urging open channels of remonstrance to nourish loyalty and filial duty; one arguing that plans for recovery must aim at complete security; and one lamenting that many gentlemen were empty and pretentious, grasping after rank and profit.

sentences.zh: 張說自閣門以節鉞簽樞密，樞方與學省同僚共論之，上雖容納而色不怡。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, from the Gate Control Office with command seal, signed into the Military Affairs Commission; Shu was just discussing this with fellow officials of the academic offices, and though the emperor accepted it his expression was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue was transferred from the Gate Control Office to sign the Military Affairs Commission with a commander's seal, Shu was discussing the appointment with colleagues in the academic offices. The emperor accepted their views but looked displeased.

sentences.zh: 樞退詣宰相，示以奏疏，且曰：「公不恥與噲等伍邪？」

translations.literal: Shu withdrew and went to the chief councilor, showed him the memorial, and said: "Are you not ashamed to be in the company of men like Kuai?"
translations.idiomatic: Shu went to the chief councilor, showed him the memorial, and said, "Are you not ashamed to keep company with men like Fan Kuai?

sentences.zh: 虞允文愧甚。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 樞即求外補，出為嚴州教授。

translations.literal: Shu at once sought an outside appointment and went out as instructor of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shu immediately sought a provincial post and was sent out as instructor at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 樞常喜誦司馬光《資治通鑒》，苦其浩博，乃區別其事而貫通之，號《通鑒紀事本末》。

translations.literal: Shu often delighted in reciting Sima Guang's Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, but was troubled by its vast scope; he therefore distinguished events and threaded them through, titling it Events in Their Entirety Based on the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Shu loved to read Sima Guang's Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government but found it unwieldy in its scope. He rearranged it by event into a connected narrative and called the work Events in Their Entirety Based on the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 參知政事龔茂良得其書，奏於上，孝宗讀而嘉歎，以賜東宮及分賜江上諸帥，且令熟讀，曰：「治道盡在是矣。」

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councilor Gong Maoliang obtained his book and memorialized it to the throne; Xiaozong read and praised it with admiration, bestowing it on the Eastern Palace and distributing copies to the commanders along the Yangzi, and ordering thorough reading, saying: "The way of governance is wholly in this."
translations.idiomatic: Vice grand councilor Gong Maoliang obtained the book and presented it to the throne. Xiaozong read it with admiration, had copies sent to the crown prince and distributed to commanders along the Yangzi, and ordered them to study it closely, saying, "The way of governance is all here."

sentences.zh: 他日，上問袁樞今何官，茂良以實對，上曰：「可與寺監簿。」

translations.literal: Another day the emperor asked what office Yuan Shu now held; Maoliang answered truthfully, and the emperor said: "He may be given a registrar post in a directorate or commission."
translations.idiomatic: On another day the emperor asked what post Yuan Shu presently held. Maoliang answered truthfully, and the emperor said, "Give him a registrar post in one of the directorates or commissions.

sentences.zh: 於是以大宗正簿召登對，即因史書以言曰：「臣竊聞陛下嘗讀《通鑒》，屢有訓詞，見諸葛亮論兩漢所以興衰，有'小人不可不去'之戒，大哉王言，垂法萬世。」

translations.literal: Thereupon, as Chief Registrar of the Great Ancestral Affairs Office, he was summoned to audience; immediately drawing on historical books he spoke, saying: "Your servant has heard that Your Majesty once read the Comprehensive Mirror and repeatedly had instructive words; seeing Zhuge Liang's discussion of why the two Han rose and fell, with the warning that 'petty men must not be left in place'—great are the king's words, a law for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: He was then summoned to audience as chief registrar of the Great Ancestral Affairs Office and spoke from history: "I have heard that when Your Majesty read the Comprehensive Mirror you often drew lessons from it. Zhuge Liang's account of why the two Han dynasties rose and fell warns that petty men must not be kept in office. What sage words—laws for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 遂曆陳往事，自漢武而下至唐文宗偏聽奸佞，致於禍亂。

translations.literal: He then went through past events in order, from Han Wudi downward to Tang Wenzong's partial listening to treacherous flatterers, leading to calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He then reviewed past reigns from Han Wudi down to Tang Wenzong, showing how partial trust in treacherous flatterers had led to disaster.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「固有詐偽而似誠實，憸佞而似忠鯁者，苟陛下日與圖事於帷幄中，進退天下士，臣恐必為朝廷累。」

translations.literal: He also said: "There are indeed deceivers who seem sincere, and crafty flatterers who seem bluntly loyal; if Your Majesty daily plotted affairs with them within the curtain, advancing and dismissing the empire's gentlemen, your servant fears they would surely become a burden to the court."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "There are deceivers who seem honest and flatterers who seem bluntly loyal. If Your Majesty daily plotted policy with such men behind closed doors and decided the fate of officials across the realm, I fear they would become a grave burden on the court.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂曰：「朕不至與此曹圖事帷幄中。」

translations.literal: The emperor turned and said: "We would not go so far as to plot affairs within the curtain with this lot."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned and said, "I would never plot policy behind closed doors with men like that.

sentences.zh: 樞謝曰：「陛下之言及此，天下之福也。」

translations.literal: Shu thanked him, saying: "That Your Majesty's words reach this point is the fortune of all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Shu thanked him and said, "That Your Majesty speaks so is a blessing for the realm."

sentences.zh: 遷太府丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director of the Court of Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 時士大夫頗有為党與者。

translations.literal: At the time many scholar-officials had formed factional affiliations.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many officials had formed factions.

sentences.zh: 樞奏曰：「人主有偏黨之心，則臣下有朋黨之患。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "When the sovereign has a partial, factional heart, then subordinates have the affliction of cliques.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized, "When the ruler favors one faction, his officials form cliques.

sentences.zh: 比年或謂陛下寵任武士，有厭薄儒生之心，猜疑大臣，親信左右，內庭行廟堂之事，近侍參軍國之謀。

translations.literal: In recent years some say Your Majesty favors and employs military men, with a mind to despise and slight Confucian scholars, suspects great ministers, trusts those at hand, lets the inner court conduct hall-of-government affairs, and lets close attendants join in military and state planning.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years some say Your Majesty favors military men and looks down on scholars, distrusts great ministers, trusts only those close at hand, lets the inner palace handle affairs of state, and allows personal attendants to join in planning war and policy.

sentences.zh: 今雖總權綱，專聽覽，而或壅蔽聰明，潛移威福。

translations.literal: Now though you hold the full reins of power and personally hear and review, yet perhaps your clear intelligence is blocked and authority and favor are secretly shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Though you now hold all authority and review affairs yourself, your judgment may still be blocked and real power quietly shifted elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 願可否惟聽於國人，毀譽不私於左右。」

translations.literal: I wish that approval and rejection be heard only from the people of the state, and that blame and praise not be kept private with those at hand."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that approval and rejection be judged by the people of the realm, and that praise and blame not be decided in private by those around you.

sentences.zh: 上方銳意北伐，示天下以所向。

translations.literal: The emperor was then keenly intent on northern expedition and showed all under Heaven where he was headed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then set on northern expedition and made his intentions plain to the realm.

sentences.zh: 樞奏：「古之謀人國者，必示之以弱，苟陛下志復金仇，臣願蓄威養銳，勿示其形。」

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "Those of old who plotted against another state always showed weakness to it; if Your Majesty's will is to avenge the Jin wrong, your servant wishes that you store up authority and nourish sharpness, and not display its form."
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized, "In antiquity those who plotted against a rival state always feigned weakness. If Your Majesty aims to avenge the Jin, I urge you to store up strength and keep your purpose hidden.

sentences.zh: 復陳用宰執、台諫之術。

translations.literal: He again set forth the methods of employing chief councilors and censorial remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: He also explained how chief councilors and censorial remonstrators should be used.

sentences.zh: 時議者欲制宗室應舉鎖試之額，限添差嶽祠，減臣僚薦舉，定文武任子，嚴特奏之等，展郊禋之歲，緩科舉之期，樞謂：「此皆近來從窄之論，人君惟天是則，不可行也。」

translations.literal: At the time debaters wished to fix quotas for imperial clansmen in locked examinations, limit supplementary appointments to mountain shrines, reduce recommendations by officials, fix civil and military hereditary privileges, tighten special-memorial promotions and the like, extend the years between suburban sacrifices, and delay the examination schedule; Shu said: "These are all recent narrow, constricting proposals; the ruler takes Heaven alone as standard—they cannot be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Some then proposed fixing quotas for imperial clansmen in locked examinations, limiting supplementary appointments to mountain shrines, reducing official recommendations, tightening rules on hereditary privileges for civil and military offices, restricting special promotions, extending the interval between suburban sacrifices, and delaying the examination schedule. Shu said, "These are all recent proposals to narrow the state. A ruler takes Heaven as his standard; such measures cannot be adopted.

sentences.zh: 遂抗疏勸上推廣大以存國體。

translations.literal: He then submitted a resisting memorial urging the emperor to extend magnanimity in order to preserve the state's proper form.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a forthright memorial urging the emperor to govern with breadth and preserve the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 兼國史院編修官，分修國史傳。

translations.literal: Concurrently he was Compilation Officer of the National History Office, assigned to compile biographies for the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as compilation officer of the National History Office, assigned to write biographies for the national history.

sentences.zh: 章惇家以其同裏，宛轉請文飾其傳，樞曰：「子厚為相，負國欺君。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun's family, because he was from the same district, circuitously asked him to embellish his biography; Shu said: "Zihou as chief councilor betrayed the state and deceived the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Because he came from the same district, Zhang Dun's family indirectly asked him to polish Zhang's biography. Shu said, "When Zihou was chief councilor he betrayed the state and deceived his ruler.

sentences.zh: 吾為史官，書法不隱，寧負鄉人，不可負天下後世公議。」

translations.literal: I am a history officer; the historian's method does not conceal—I would rather fail my fellow townsman than fail the public judgment of all under Heaven and later ages."
translations.idiomatic: I am a historian, and historians do not conceal the truth. I would rather wrong a neighbor than wrong the judgment of the world and of posterity.

sentences.zh: 時相趙雄總史事，見之歎曰：「無愧古良史。」

translations.literal: The chief councilor of the time, Zhao Xiong, who oversaw history affairs, saw this and sighed, saying: "He does not shame the good historians of old."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiong, the chief councilor then in charge of the history office, read this and sighed, "He is worthy of the great historians of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 權工部郎官，累遷兼吏部郎官。

translations.literal: He acted as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and, after successive promotions, concurrently served as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting bureau director in the Ministry of Works and was later promoted to concurrent bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 兩淮旱，命廉視真、楊、廬、和四郡。

translations.literal: When the Two Huai suffered drought, he was ordered to inspect with integrity Zhen, Yang, Lu, and He—the four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the Two Huai region, he was ordered to inspect relief in Zhen, Yang, Lu, and He prefectures.

sentences.zh: 歸陳兩淮形勢，謂：「兩淮堅固則長江可守，今徒知備江，不知保淮，置重兵於江南，委空城於淮上，非所以戒不虞。

translations.literal: Returning, he set forth the Two Huai's strategic situation, saying: "If the Two Huai are firm, the Yangzi can be defended; now you only know to prepare the river and do not know to secure the Huai, placing heavy troops in Jiangnan and leaving empty cities on the Huai—this is not the way to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he explained the strategic situation on the Two Huai and said, "If the Two Huai are secure, the Yangzi can be held. Now the court knows only how to defend the river and not how to hold the Huai, massing troops south of the Yangzi while leaving empty cities on the north bank. That is no way to guard against surprise.

sentences.zh: 瓜洲新城，專為退保，金使過而指議，淮人聞而歎嗟。

translations.literal: The new city at Guazhou was built solely for retreat and defense; Jin envoys passed and pointed and discussed it, and Huai people heard and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: The new fort at Guazhou was built only as a fallback position. Jin envoys passed by and mocked it, and people on the Huai sighed when they heard.

sentences.zh: 誰為陛下建此策也？」

translations.literal: Who for Your Majesty devised this strategy?"
translations.idiomatic: Who advised Your Majesty to adopt this policy?"

sentences.zh: 遷軍器少監，除提舉江東常平茶鹽，改知處州，赴闕奏事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Armory, appointed intendant of Jiangdong Ever-Normal Granaries, Tea, and Salt, then changed to prefect of Chu Prefecture and went to court to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Armory, appointed intendant of Jiangdong ever-normal granaries, tea, and salt, then transferred to prefect of Chuzhou and summoned to court to report on affairs.

sentences.zh: 樞之使淮入對也，嘗言：「朋黨相附則大臣之權重，言路壅塞則人主之勢孤。」

translations.literal: When Shu, on his Huai mission, entered audience, he had once said: "When factions attach to one another, great ministers' power grows heavy; when the path of speech is blocked, the sovereign's position stands alone."
translations.idiomatic: When Shu had gone to the Huai region and appeared at audience, he had said, "When factions band together, chief ministers grow too powerful; when remonstrance is blocked, the ruler stands alone.

sentences.zh: 時宰不悅。

translations.literal: The chief councilor of the time was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 至是又言：「威權在下則主勢弱，故大臣逐台諫以蔽人主之聰明；

translations.literal: At this point he again said: "When authority rests below, the sovereign's position is weak; therefore great ministers drive out censors and remonstrators to block the sovereign's clear intelligence;
translations.idiomatic: Now he said again, "When power lies below, the ruler is weak, so great ministers drive out censors and remonstrators to blind the throne;

sentences.zh: 威權在上則主勢強，故大臣結台諫以遏天下之公議。

translations.literal: when authority rests above, the sovereign's position is strong; therefore great ministers bind censors and remonstrators to choke off public opinion under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: when power rests above, the ruler is strong, so great ministers bind censors and remonstrators to choke off public opinion across the realm.

sentences.zh: 今朋黨之舊尚在，台諫之官未正紀綱，言路將復荊榛矣。」

translations.literal: Now the old factional ties still remain, the offices of censors and remonstrators have not set right discipline and measure, and the path of speech will again become thorn and bramble."
translations.idiomatic: The old factions still survive, censors and remonstrators no longer uphold proper discipline, and the path of remonstrance will soon be choked with weeds again."

sentences.zh: 除吏部員外郎，遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Outer Assistant in the Ministry of Personnel and transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed outer assistant in the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 通州民高氏以產業事下大理，殿中侍御史冷世光納厚賂曲庇之，樞直其事以聞，人為危之。

translations.literal: A man of Tong Prefecture surnamed Gao, over a property affair, was sent down to the Court of Judicial Review; Palace Attendant Censor Leng Shiguang took heavy bribes and bent protection to him; Shu reported the facts directly to the throne, and people worried for him.
translations.idiomatic: When a property dispute involving a Tongzhou man surnamed Gao reached the Court of Judicial Review, Palace Attendant Censor Leng Shiguang took heavy bribes and shielded him. Shu reported the facts directly to the emperor, and many feared for his safety.

sentences.zh: 上怒，立罷世光，以朝臣劾御史，實自樞始。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and immediately dismissed Shiguang; that a court minister impeached a censor in fact began with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and immediately dismissed Shiguang. The precedent of a court minister impeaching a censor began with Shu.

sentences.zh: 手詔權工部侍郎，仍兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: By handwritten edict he was made Acting Vice Minister of Works, still concurrently Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: By handwritten edict he was made acting vice minister of works while continuing as director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 因論大理獄案請外，有予郡之命，既而貶兩秩，寢前旨。

translations.literal: Because of the Dali prison case he requested an outer post; there was an order granting a prefecture, but then he was demoted two ranks and the previous edict was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the Dali case he asked for a provincial post. An order granting him a prefecture was issued, but he was then demoted two ranks and the earlier appointment was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 光宗受禪，敘復元官，提舉太平興國宮、知常德府。

translations.literal: When Guangzong received the abdication, his original rank was restored by seniority; he was made intendant of the Taiping Xingguo Palace and prefect of Changde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended the throne, Shu was restored to his former rank and appointed intendant of the Taiping Xingguo Palace and prefect of Changde.

sentences.zh: 自是閒居十載，作《易傳解義》及《辯異》、《童子問》等書藏於家。

translations.literal: From then he lived in retirement for ten years, composing Explanatory Meaning of the Changes Commentary, Distinguishing Divergences, Questions of the Young Student, and other books kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: He then lived in retirement for ten years, writing Explanatory Meaning of the Changes Commentary, Distinguishing Divergences, Questions of the Young Student, and other works that he kept at home.

sentences.zh: 李椿，字壽翁，洺州永年人。

translations.literal: Li Chun, courtesy name Shouweng, was a native of Yongnian in Mo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chun, whose courtesy name was Shouweng, came from Yongnian in Mo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父升，進士起家。

translations.literal: His father Sheng entered office through the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Sheng had entered office as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 靖康之難，升翼其父，以背受刃，與長子俱卒。

translations.literal: In the disaster of Jingkang, Sheng shielded his father, taking the blade on his back, and died together with the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: During the disaster of Jingkang, Sheng shielded his father with his back and took the blade; he and his eldest son both died.

sentences.zh: 椿年尚幼，藁殯佛寺，深竁而詳識之；

translations.literal: Chun was still young; they coffined the bodies in straw at a Buddhist temple and buried them deep with detailed markers;
translations.idiomatic: Chun was still a boy. The bodies were coffined in straw at a Buddhist temple and buried deep with careful markers;

sentences.zh: 奉繼母南走，艱苦備嘗，竭力以養。

translations.literal: he accompanied his stepmother fleeing south, tasted every hardship, and with full effort supported her.
translations.idiomatic: he fled south with his stepmother, endured every hardship, and did all he could to support her.

sentences.zh: 以父澤，補迪功郎，曆官至甯國軍節度推官。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he was granted Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement and rose through offices to Military Push Officer of the Ningguo Army command.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he received the rank of gentleman for meritorious achievement and rose to serve as military push officer of the Ningguo Army command.

sentences.zh: 治豪民偽券，還陳氏田，吏才精強，人稱之。

translations.literal: Handling a powerful man's forged deed, he returned the Chen family's land; his administrative talent was keen and strong, and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he handled a powerful man's forged deed and restored land to the Chen family, people praised his sharp administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 張浚辟為制司準備差遣，常以自隨。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun recruited him as staff preparation officer of the pacification commission and often kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun recruited him as a staff preparation officer on the pacification commission and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 椿奔走淮甸，綏流民，布屯戍，察廬、壽軍情，相視山水砦險要，周密精審，所助為多。

translations.literal: Chun rushed about the Huai region, settling displaced people, deploying garrison colonies, inspecting military conditions at Lu and Shou, and surveying mountain-and-water strongpoints and strategic passes—thorough, precise, and careful; the help he gave was great.
translations.idiomatic: Chun traveled tirelessly across the Huai region, resettling displaced people, organizing garrison colonies, inspecting troop conditions at Luzhou and Shouzhou, and surveying mountain passes and strategic strongpoints with meticulous care. His assistance was considerable.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年春，諸將有以北討之議上聞者，事下督府，椿方奉檄至巢，亟奏記浚曰：「復讎伐敵，天下大義，不出督府而出諸將，況藩籬不固，儲備不豐，將多而非才，兵弱而未練，議論不定，縱得其地，未易守也。」

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Longxing, when generals had a proposal for northern expedition reported upward, the matter was sent down to the supervisory headquarters; Chun had just received orders and reached Chao, and urgently submitted a letter to Jun saying: "Avenging wrongs and attacking the enemy is the great righteousness of all under Heaven, yet it is not coming from the supervisory headquarters but from the generals; moreover the frontier bulwark is not firm, stores and preparations are not ample, generals are many but not talented, troops are weak and not yet trained, and opinion is unsettled—even if you gain the territory, it will not be easy to hold."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Longxing, when generals proposed a northern campaign and the matter reached the supervisory headquarters, Chun had just arrived at Chao on orders from Zhang Jun. He urgently wrote to Jun: "Recovering lost territory and striking the enemy is the great duty of the realm. Yet the plan comes not from headquarters but from the generals. The frontier is not secure, supplies are insufficient, the generals are numerous but untalented, the troops weak and untrained, and opinion divided. Even if ground is taken, it will be hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 既而師出無功。

translations.literal: Soon after the army went out without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched north and achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 浚嘗歎實才之難，椿曰：「豈可厚誣天下無人，唯不惡逆耳而甘遜志，則庶其肯來耳。」

translations.literal: Jun once sighed at how hard real talent was to find; Chun said: "How can one heavily slander that there are no men under Heaven? Only if you do not hate straight speech and are willing to humble your will, then perhaps they will be willing to come."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun once lamented how hard it was to find real talent. Chun said, "You cannot fairly claim there are no capable men in the realm. Only if you do not resent blunt counsel and are willing to humble yourself will they be willing to come.

sentences.zh: 浚復除右相，椿知事不可為，勸之去。

translations.literal: Jun was again appointed right chief councilor; Chun knew affairs could not be accomplished and urged him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was again appointed right chief councilor, Chun saw that nothing could be done and urged him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 明年春，浚出視師，椿曰：「小人之黨已勝，公無故去朝廷，蹤跡必危。」

translations.literal: The next spring, when Jun went out to inspect the army, Chun said: "The faction of petty men has already prevailed; if you leave the court without cause, your track will surely be perilous."
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, when Jun went out to inspect the army, Chun said, "The faction of petty men has already won. If you leave the capital without urgent cause, your position will surely become dangerous.

sentences.zh: 復申前說甚苦。

translations.literal: He again pressed his earlier argument with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his earlier argument with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 浚心是之，而自以宗臣任天下之重，不忍決去，未幾果罷。

translations.literal: Jun agreed in his heart, but considering himself a dynastic minister bearing the weight of all under Heaven, he could not bear to decide to leave; before long he was indeed dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun agreed in his heart, but as a dynastic elder bearing the weight of the realm he could not bring himself to withdraw. Before long he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 監登聞鼓院，有所不樂，請通判廉州以歸。

translations.literal: As overseer of the Petition Drum Court, discontented with something, he requested vice prefect of Lian Prefecture in order to return home.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as overseer of the Petition Drum Court he grew unhappy with his situation and asked to be made vice prefect of Lianzhou so he could return south.

sentences.zh: 未上，召對，知鄂州。

translations.literal: Before the request went up, he was summoned to audience and made prefect of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before the request was submitted, he was summoned to audience and appointed prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 請行墾田，復戶數千，曠士大辟。

translations.literal: He requested to carry out reclamation farming, restored several thousand households, and greatly opened up idle land.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to launch land reclamation, restored several thousand households, and greatly opened up abandoned fields.

sentences.zh: 移廣西提點刑獄，獄未竟者，一以平決之，釋所疑數十百人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangxi intendant of judicial inspection; for cases not yet concluded he uniformly decided them fairly and released several score or hundred persons of doubtful guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guangxi as intendant of judicial inspection. For all unfinished cases he rendered fair judgments and released several dozen to a hundred people whose guilt was uncertain.

sentences.zh: 奏罷昭州金坑，禁仕者毋市南物。

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish the gold mines of Zhao Prefecture and forbade officeholders from buying southern goods.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to shut down the gold mines in Zhaozhou and banned officials from purchasing goods from the south.

sentences.zh: 移湖北漕，適歲大侵，官強民振糶，且下其價，米不至，益艱食。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hubei transport commissioner; just then the year had a great famine; the government forced the people to sell grain compulsorily and also lowered the price; rice did not arrive, and food grew even scarcer.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hubei grain intendant. That year brought severe famine. The government forced merchants to sell grain at compulsory prices and cut those prices further, but grain still did not arrive and food grew even scarcer.

sentences.zh: 椿損所強糶數而不遏其直，未幾米舟湊集，價減十三。

translations.literal: Chun reduced the quantity of compulsory sales without restraining the market price; before long rice boats gathered in number, and the price fell by three tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Chun cut the amount of grain the government forced merchants to sell without capping prices. Before long boats loaded with rice gathered in port, and prices fell by thirty percent.

sentences.zh: 每行部，必前期戒吏具州縣所當問事列為籍，單車以行，所至取吏卒備使令。

translations.literal: Whenever he toured his jurisdiction, he always beforehand admonished clerks to prepare a register listing matters each prefecture and county should be questioned on; he traveled alone in a single cart, and wherever he arrived took local clerks and soldiers as attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he made a tour of inspection, he sent word in advance that clerks should draw up a register of matters to raise with each prefecture and county. He traveled alone in a single cart and, at each stop, took local clerks and soldiers to serve him.

sentences.zh: 凡以例致饋，一不受，言事者請下諸道為式。

translations.literal: All gifts given according to custom he would not accept a single one; memorialists asked that this be sent down to all circuits as a model.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every customary gift offered to him. Memorialists asked that his practice be issued to all circuits as a standard.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部郎官，論廣西鹽法，孝宗是其說，遂改法焉。

translations.literal: He was summoned as a bureau official of the Ministry of Personnel; he discussed the Guangxi salt law; Xiaozong approved his argument and thereupon changed the law.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve in the Ministry of Personnel. He argued for reform of the Guangxi salt law. Xiaozong accepted his proposal and changed the law accordingly.

sentences.zh: 除樞密院檢詳。

translations.literal: He was appointed detailed examiner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed detailed examiner in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 小吏持南丹州莫酋表，求自宜州市馬者，因簽書張說以聞。

translations.literal: A minor clerk held a memorial from the Mo chieftain of Nandan Prefecture requesting to buy horses from Yizhou City, and through signing secretary Zhang Shuo reported it upward.
translations.idiomatic: A minor clerk brought a memorial from the Mo chieftain of Nandan Prefecture asking permission to purchase horses at Yizhou. He passed it up through signing secretary Zhang Shuo.

sentences.zh: 椿謂：「邕遠宜近，故遷之，豈無意？

translations.literal: Chun said: "Yong is far and Yizhou is near—he was transferred for that reason; can there be no intention?
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "Yongzhou is far and Yizhou is near—that is why he was transferred. Can there be no deeper purpose?

sentences.zh: 今莫氏方橫，奈何道之以中國地裏之近？

translations.literal: Now the Mo clan is just now unruly—how can one tell them of the nearness of Chinese territory in terms of distance?
translations.idiomatic: The Mo clan is growing bold. How can we tell them how close Chinese territory lies?

sentences.zh: 小吏妄作，將啟邊釁，請論如法。」

translations.literal: The minor clerk acted recklessly and will open a border provocation; I ask that he be punished according to law."
translations.idiomatic: This clerk acted recklessly and could provoke a border incident. I ask that he be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 說怒，椿因求去，上慰諭令安職。

translations.literal: Shuo was angry; Chun thereupon requested to leave; the emperor consoled and instructed him to keep his post in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was angry. Chun then asked to resign. The emperor consoled him and told him to remain at his post.

sentences.zh: 遷左司，復請外，除直龍圖閣、湖南運副。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left bureau director; again requested an outside post; appointed direct associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall and vice transport commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left bureau director but again asked for an outside appointment. He was made direct associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall and vice transport commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 兼請十三事，同日報可，大者減桂陽軍月樁錢萬二千緡，損民稅折銀之直，民刻石紀之。

translations.literal: He also submitted thirteen requests; on the same day all were approved. The greatest was reducing Guiyang Army's monthly pole money by twelve thousand strings of cash and reducing the assessment on the people's tax conversion to silver; the people carved stone to record it.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted thirteen petitions, all approved the same day. The most important reduced Guiyang Army's monthly pole tax by twelve thousand strings of cash and cut the surcharge on converting tax payments to silver. The people carved his deed in stone.

sentences.zh: 除司農卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed director of the Court of the National Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Court of the National Granary.

sentences.zh: 椿會大農歲用米百七十萬斛，而省倉見米僅支一二月，歎曰：「真所謂國非其國矣。」

translations.literal: Chun calculated that the granary administration used 1.7 million hu of rice annually, yet the provincial granary's rice on hand could support only one or two months, and sighed: "Truly what is called—the state is not its state."
translations.idiomatic: Chun noted that the granary administration consumed 1.7 million hu of rice each year, yet the provincial stores held barely one or two months' supply. He sighed, "This is truly what people mean when they say the state is no longer a state.

sentences.zh: 力請歲儲二百萬斛為一年之蓄。

translations.literal: He vigorously requested annual storage of two million hu as one year's reserve.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently petitioned to store two million hu each year as a year's reserve.

sentences.zh: 擇臨安守，椿在議中，執政或謂其於人無委曲，上曰：「正欲得如此人。」

translations.literal: In selecting the prefect of Lin'an, Chun was among those considered; a chief councilor said perhaps he was not accommodating toward people; the emperor said: "I precisely want to get such a man."
translations.idiomatic: When choosing a prefect for Lin'an, Chun was among the candidates. A chief councilor remarked that he was not accommodating toward others. The emperor said, "That is precisely the kind of man I want.

sentences.zh: 遂兼臨安府，視事三月，竟以幸不便解去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he also took Lin'an Prefecture; after holding office three months, in the end because the imperial tour was inconvenient he was relieved and left.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to govern Lin'an as well. After three months in office he was dismissed because his presence made an imperial tour inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 椿在朝，遇事輒言，執政故不悅。

translations.literal: Chun at court, whenever there was a matter would speak out; the chief councilors therefore were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: While at court Chun spoke out on every issue that arose, and the chief councilors disliked him for it.

sentences.zh: 及是轉對，又言：「君以剛健為體而虛中為用，臣以柔順為體而剛中為用。

translations.literal: At this rotating remonstrance audience, he again said: "The sovereign takes firm vigor as substance and empty-centeredness as function; the minister takes yielding compliance as substance and firm-centeredness as function.
translations.idiomatic: At a rotating remonstrance audience he said again, "The ruler's substance is firm vigor and his practice is receptive openness. The minister's substance is yielding compliance and his practice is firm integrity within.

sentences.zh: 陛下得虛中之道，以行剛健之德矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has obtained the Way of empty-centeredness to carry out the virtue of firm vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has mastered receptive openness and thereby exercises firm, vigorous rule.

sentences.zh: 在廷之臣，未見其能以剛中守柔順而事陛下者也。」

translations.literal: The ministers at court—I have not seen any who can, with firm-centeredness, preserve yielding compliance in serving Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: I see no minister at court who upholds yielding deference with firm integrity in serving Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 執政滋不悅，出知婺州。

translations.literal: The chief councilors grew even more displeased; he was sent out as prefect of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilors grew still more displeased. He was sent out to serve as prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會詔市牛筋，凡五千斤。

translations.literal: Just then an edict ordered the purchase of ox sinew, totaling five thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the purchase of five thousand jin of ox sinew.

sentences.zh: 椿奏：「一牛之筋才四兩，是欲屠二萬牛也。」

translations.literal: Chun memorialized: "One ox's sinew is only four liang; this means wanting to slaughter twenty thousand oxen."
translations.idiomatic: Chun memorialized, "One ox yields only four liang of sinew. This order would require slaughtering twenty thousand oxen.

sentences.zh: 上悟，為收前詔。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and thereupon withdrew the previous edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and rescinded the edict.

sentences.zh: 除吏部侍郎，又極言閽寺之盛，曰：「自古宦官之盛衰，系國家興亡。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel; he again spoke exhaustively of the flourishing of eunuch offices, saying: "From antiquity the rise and fall of eunuchs has been tied to the rise and fall of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and again spoke forcefully against the power of eunuch offices. He said, "Since antiquity the rise and fall of eunuchs has been bound up with the fate of the state.

sentences.zh: 其盛也，始則人畏之，甚則人惡之，極則群起而攻之。

translations.literal: When they flourish, at first people fear them; at length people hate them; at the extreme the masses rise together to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When they grow powerful, people first fear them, then hate them, and in the end rise up together against them.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐勿論，靖康、明受之禍未遠，必有以裁制之，不使至極，則國家免於前日之患，宦官亦保其富貴。

translations.literal: Leave aside Han and Tang; the disasters of Jingkang and Mingshou are not distant—we must have means to restrain them and not let them reach the extreme; then the state will be spared yesterday's calamity, and the eunuchs too will preserve their wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Set aside Han and Tang—the catastrophes of Jingkang and Mingshou are still recent. Eunuch power must be checked before it reaches its extreme. Then the state will be spared such disasters, and the eunuchs themselves will keep their wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 門禁宮戒之外，勿得預外事，嚴禁士大夫兵將官與之交通。」

translations.literal: Outside palace gate prohibition and inner palatial security, they must not interfere in outside affairs; strictly forbid scholar-officials and military generals from associating with them."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond palace gate duties and inner security, they must not meddle in outside affairs. Scholar-officials and military officers must be strictly forbidden to have dealings with them.

sentences.zh: 上聞靖康、明受語，蹙頞久之，曰：「幼亦聞此。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard the words Jingkang and Mingshou, he furrowed his brow a long time and said: "In youth I also heard this."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard him mention Jingkang and Mingshou, he furrowed his brow for a long moment and said, "I heard the same in my youth.

sentences.zh: 因納疏袖中以入。

translations.literal: He then took the memorial into his sleeve and entered.
translations.idiomatic: He then put the memorial in his sleeve and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 最後極言：「當預邊備，如欲保淮，則楚州、盱眙、昭信、濠梁、渦口、花靨、正陽、光州皆不可以不守；

translations.literal: Finally he spoke exhaustively: "One should prepare border defenses in advance; if one wishes to hold the Huai, then Chuzhou, Xuyi, Zhaoxin, Haoliang, Wokou, Huaye, Zhengyang, and Guangzhou—all cannot be left undefended;
translations.idiomatic: Finally he spoke at length on border preparedness. "If the Huai is to be held, Chuzhou, Xuyi, Zhaoxin, Haoliang, Wokou, Huaye, Zhengyang, and Guangzhou must all be defended.

sentences.zh: 如欲保江，則高郵、六合、瓦梁、濡須、巢湖、北峽亦要地也。」

translations.literal: If one wishes to hold the Yangtze, then Gaoyou, Liuhe, Waliang, Ruxu, Chaohu, and Beixia are also vital places."
translations.idiomatic: If the Yangtze is to be held, Gaoyou, Liuhe, Waliang, Ruxu, Chaohu, and Beixia are vital as well."

sentences.zh: 以病請祠，不許，面請益力，乃除集英殿修撰、知甯國府，改太平州，賜尚方珍劑以遣。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested a sinecure post; not permitted; he pleaded in person with greater force; thereupon appointed Hanlin Academy compiler and prefect of Ningguo Prefecture, changed to Taiping Prefecture, and bestowed precious medicines from the imperial pharmacy to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a sinecure post on grounds of illness but was refused. He pleaded in person still more forcefully and was appointed Hanlin Academy compiler and prefect of Ningguo, then transferred to Taiping Prefecture, with precious medicines from the imperial pharmacy sent to see him off.

sentences.zh: 既至，力圖上流之備，請選將練習，緩急列艦，上可以援東關、濡須，下可以應採石。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he vigorously planned upper-stream defenses, requested selection of generals for training, and deployment of warships for emergencies—upstream able to aid Dongguan and Ruxu, downstream able to respond at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: Once there he worked hard to strengthen the upper Yangtze defenses. He requested that generals be chosen and trained and warships arranged for emergencies—able to support Dongguan and Ruxu upstream and respond at Caishi downstream.

sentences.zh: 年六十九，上章請老，以敷文閣待制致仕。

translations.literal: At age sixty-nine he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; as a Hanlin academy editing compiler he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty-nine he memorialized to retire and was granted retirement as a Hanlin academy editing compiler.

sentences.zh: 越再歲，上念湖南兵役之餘，欲鎮安之，謂椿重厚可倚，命待制顯謨閣、知潭州、湖南安撫使。

translations.literal: After two more years, the emperor, mindful that Hunan still suffered the aftermath of military service, wished to pacify and settle it; considering Chun solid and dependable, he ordered him Hanlin academy editing compiler of the Xianmo Hall, prefect of Tan Prefecture, and Hunan pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor, mindful that Hunan still bore the scars of military service, wished to pacify the region. Considering Chun solid and trustworthy, he appointed him Hanlin academy compiler of the Xianmo Hall, prefect of Tanzhou, and Hunan pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累辭不獲，乃勉起，至則撫摩凋瘵，氣象一如盛時。

translations.literal: Repeatedly declining but not obtaining permission, he then reluctantly rose; upon arrival he comforted the exhausted and afflicted, and the atmosphere was again as in flourishing times.
translations.idiomatic: He declined repeatedly but could not refuse. He reluctantly took the post, and on arrival comforted the war-ravaged populace until the region's spirit matched its most prosperous days.

sentences.zh: 復酒稅法，人以為便。

translations.literal: He restored the wine tax law; people considered it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the wine tax law, which people found convenient.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，發廩勸分，蠲租十一萬，糶常平米二萬，活數萬人。

translations.literal: In a year of drought, he opened granaries and encouraged sharing, remitted one hundred ten thousand in rent, sold twenty thousand hu from regular ever-normal granaries, and saved several ten-thousands of people.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought he opened granaries and urged mutual aid, remitted one hundred ten thousand in rent, sold twenty thousand hu from the ever-normal granaries, and saved tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 潭新置飛虎軍，或以為非便，椿曰：「長沙一都會，控扼湖、嶺，鎮撫蠻徭，二十年間，大盜三起，何可無一軍？

translations.literal: Tan had newly established the Flying Tiger Army; some considered it inconvenient; Chun said: "Changsha is a great metropolis, controlling Hunan and the mountain ranges, pacifying Man and Yao—within twenty years great bandits rose three times; how can there be no army?
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhou had recently established the Flying Tiger Army. Some said it was unnecessary. Chun said, "Changsha is a major city controlling Hunan and the mountain frontier and pacifying Man and Yao peoples. In twenty years major bandit uprisings have occurred three times. How can the region do without an army?

sentences.zh: 且已費縣官緡錢四十二萬，何可廢耶？

translations.literal: Moreover already forty-two ten-thousands of strings of official cash have been spent—how can it be abolished?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, four hundred twenty thousand strings of official funds have already been spent. How can it be abolished?

sentences.zh: 亦在馭之而已。」

translations.literal: It is only a matter of controlling them, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The question is simply how to command them properly.

sentences.zh: 未滿歲，復告歸，進敷文閣直學士致仕，朝拜命，夕登舟，歸老野塘上。

translations.literal: Before a full year he again reported wishing to return; advanced to Hanlin academy direct academician in retirement; in the morning received the appointment, at evening boarded a boat, and returned to old age on Wild Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Before a full year had passed he asked to retire again. He was promoted to Hanlin academy direct academician and granted retirement. He received the appointment in the morning, boarded a boat that evening, and returned to live out his old age on Wild Pond.

sentences.zh: 椿年十五歲避地南來，貧無以為養，不得專力於學。

translations.literal: Chun at age fifteen fled south as a refugee; poor with no means to support himself, he could not devote himself wholly to study.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Chun fled south as a refugee. Too poor to support himself, he could not devote himself fully to study.

sentences.zh: 年三十始學《易》，其言於朝廷，措諸行事，皆《易》之用。

translations.literal: At age thirty he began studying the Changes; his words at court and his application in action were all uses of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He did not begin studying the Book of Changes until thirty. His counsel at court and his conduct in office were all applications of that text.

sentences.zh: 嶷然有守，存心每主于厚，尤惡佛老邪說。

translations.literal: Towering in integrity, his mind always took thickness as lord; he especially hated Buddhist and Daoist heterodox doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: He stood firm in principle, always inclined toward generosity of spirit, and especially despised Buddhist and Daoist heterodox teachings.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十年，卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chunxi he died, age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Chunxi, at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 朱熹嘗銘其墓，謂其「逆知得失，不假蓍龜」，「不阿主好，不詭時譽」云。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi once inscribed his tomb, saying of him "foreknowing gain and loss without relying on yarrow stalks and tortoise shells," "not flattering the sovereign's preferences, not deviously pursuing timely reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi once composed his tomb inscription, praising him for "foreseeing gain and loss without divining sticks or shells" and for "never flattering the ruler's preferences or currying favor with the times."

sentences.zh: 劉儀鳳

translations.literal: Liu Yifeng
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yifeng

sentences.zh: 劉儀鳳，字韶美，普州人。

translations.literal: Liu Yifeng, styled Shaomei, was a man of Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yifeng, styled Shaomei, was from Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以文謁左丞馮澥，澥甚推許，遂知名。

translations.literal: In youth with his writing he called on Left Vice Grand Councilor Feng Xie; Xie greatly praised and approved him, and he thereupon became known.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he presented his writings to Left Vice Grand Councilor Feng Xie, who praised him highly, and he soon became known.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，登進士第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 抱負倜儻，不事生產，於仕進恬如也。

translations.literal: His ambitions were free and bold; he did not attend to productive work; toward official advancement he was calm and indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and unconventional in spirit, he cared nothing for worldly gain and was indifferent to office and promotion.

sentences.zh: 擢第十年，始赴調，尉遂寧府之蓬溪，監資州資陽縣酒稅，為果州、榮州掾。

translations.literal: Ten years after passing the examination he first went to receive appointment; he was assistant magistrate of Pengxi in Suining Prefecture, overseer of wine tax at Ziyang County in Zi Prefecture, and staff officer of Guo and Rong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years after passing the examination he first sought appointment, serving as assistant magistrate of Pengxi in Suining Prefecture, overseer of wine tax at Ziyang in Zizhou, and staff officer in Guo and Rong prefectures.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十七年，有旨令侍從薦士，起居郎趙逵舉儀鳳，稱其「富有詞華，恬於進取。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing, an order directed attendant officials to recommend men of talent; Attendant Gentleman Zhao Kui recommended Yifeng, saying of him "rich in literary elegance, calm about advancement."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing the emperor ordered attendant officials to recommend talented men. Attendant Gentleman Zhao Kui recommended Yifeng, praising his "literary elegance and indifference to advancement.

sentences.zh: 宰執上其名，上曰：「蜀人道遠，文學行義有可用者，不由論薦，何緣知之？

translations.literal: The chief councilors submitted his name; the emperor said: "Shu people—the road is far; those with usable learning and conduct in letters—without recommendation through discussion, by what means would one know them?
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilors submitted his name. The emperor said, "Shu is far away. How are men of literary talent and moral worth to be known if they cannot reach us except through recommendation?

sentences.zh: 前此蜀仕宦者例多隔絕，不得一至朝廷，殊可惜也。」

translations.literal: Before this Sichuan officeholders as a rule were mostly cut off and could not once reach the court—a great pity indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Until now officials from Shu had largely been cut off from court and rarely reached the capital. That is a great pity.

sentences.zh: 自秦檜專權，深抑蜀士，故上語及之。

translations.literal: Since Qin Gui monopolized power and deeply suppressed Shu scholars, the emperor's words touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin Gui had monopolized power and deeply suppressed scholars from Shu, the emperor's remark referred to that.

sentences.zh: 尋除諸王宮大小學教授。

translations.literal: Soon appointed professor of the great and small schools of the Princes' Establishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed professor in the great and small schools of the princes' establishments.

sentences.zh: 召試館職，辭以久離場屋，改國子監丞。

translations.literal: Summoned to examination for a library post; he declined on grounds of long separation from the examination hall; changed to Assistant Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the library service examination but declined, saying he had been away from the examination halls too long. He was made assistant director of the Directorate of Education instead.

sentences.zh: 宰相以其名士，遷秘書丞、禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: The chief councilor, because he was a famous scholar, promoted him to secretary director and foreign service vice director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was a noted scholar, the chief councilor promoted him to secretary director and vice director of rites in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 所草箋奏，以典雅稱。

translations.literal: The memorials and reports he drafted were praised for classical elegance.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials he drafted were praised for their classical elegance.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，議上「光堯壽聖」尊號冊寶，有欲俟欽宗服除者，太常博士林栗謂：「唐憲宗上順宗冊寶在德宗服中，不必避，備樂而不作可也。」

translations.literal: When Xiaozong received the abdication, they debated presenting the honorific title and seal and regalia "Guangyao Shousheng"; some wished to wait until Qinzong's mourning period ended; Taichang doctor Lin Li said: "When Tang Xianzong presented Shunzong's honorific seal during Dezong's mourning, avoidance was not necessary—prepare music but do not perform it, that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne, the court debated presenting the honorific title and regalia "Guangyao Shousheng." Some wished to wait until mourning for Emperor Qinzong had ended. Taichang doctor Lin Li argued, "When Tang Xianzong presented Emperor Shunzong's honorific seal during Dezong's mourning, no avoidance was required. Music could be prepared but not performed.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳獨上議曰：「謹按上尊號事屬嘉禮，累朝必俟郊祀慶成然後舉行。

translations.literal: Yifeng alone submitted an opinion saying: "Carefully examining the matter, presenting an honorific title belongs to auspicious ritual; successive dynasties always waited until the suburban sacrifice celebration was complete before carrying it out.
translations.idiomatic: Yifeng alone submitted a dissent, arguing, "Presenting an honorific title is an auspicious rite. Successive dynasties always waited until the suburban sacrifice had been completed.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝為欽宗備禮終制，見於詔書。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor prepared full mourning rites for Qinzong to the end of the prescribed period—this appears in the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor's edicts show that he observed full mourning rites for Emperor Qinzong.

sentences.zh: 議者引憲宗故事，考之唐史，自武德以來，皆用易月之制，與本朝事體大相遠也。

translations.literal: The debaters cite Xianzong's precedent; examining Tang history, from Wude onward all used the shortened-month system—greatly far from this dynasty's situation in substance.
translations.idiomatic: Those who cite Xianzong's precedent should examine Tang history. From the Wude era onward the court used shortened mourning. That practice differs greatly from our dynasty's customs.

sentences.zh: 乞候欽宗終制，檢舉以行，則國家盛美，主上事親情實稱矣。」

translations.literal: I beg to wait until Qinzong's mourning period ends, investigate and carry it out—then the state's grandeur will be complete and the sovereign's filial sincerity toward parents will be truly fitting."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we wait until mourning for Qinzong is complete and then proceed accordingly. The state's glory will be preserved and Your Majesty's filial conduct will be rightly expressed.

sentences.zh: 議者雖是其言，然謂事親當權宜而從厚，竟用栗議，儀鳳復爭辨不已。

translations.literal: The debaters though agreeing with his words, yet said that in serving parents one should use expedience and follow the more generous course; in the end they used Li's proposal; Yifeng again argued without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Though some agreed with him, they held that filial duty should be interpreted generously. Li's proposal was adopted in the end, and Yifeng continued to argue without stopping.

sentences.zh: 尋兼國史院編修官兼權秘書少監。

translations.literal: Soon additionally State History Academy compiler and acting vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a compiler in the State History Academy and acting vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，遷兵部侍郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao, promoted to vice minister of war and concurrently court lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiandao he was promoted to vice minister of war and court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳在朝十年，每歸即匿其車騎，扃其門戶，客至，無親疏皆不得見，政府累月始一上謁，人尤其傲，奉入，半以儲書，凡萬餘卷，國史錄無遺者。

translations.literal: Yifeng was at court ten years; whenever he returned he hid his carriage and horses and bolted his doors; when guests came, whether close or distant none could see him; at the chief councilor's office he went up to pay respects only once in many months—people especially blamed his arrogance; of his salary half went to storing books, totaling more than ten thousand scrolls, with nothing omitted from the state history records.
translations.idiomatic: Yifeng served at court for ten years. Whenever he returned home he hid his carriage and horses and bolted his doors. Guests, close or distant alike, could not see him. He visited the chief councilor's office only once in many months, and people chiefly blamed his arrogance. He spent half his salary on books, amassing more than ten thousand scrolls, including complete copies of the state history records.

sentences.zh: 御史張之綱論儀鳳錄四庫書本以傳私室，遂斥歸蜀。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Zhigang accused Yifeng of copying Four Repositories books to spread to his private house; he was thereupon dismissed and sent back to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Zhigang accused Yifeng of copying books from the Four Repositories for his private collection. He was dismissed and sent back to Shu.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，輔臣進前侍從當復職者，上曰：「劉儀鳳無罪，可與復集英殿修撰。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year, assisting ministers presented former attendants who should be restored to office; the emperor said: "Liu Yifeng is without guilt; he may be restored as Hanlin Academy compiler of the Hall for Cherishing Worthies."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year the chief ministers presented names of former attendants due for restoration. The emperor said, "Liu Yifeng is innocent. Restore him as Hanlin Academy compiler of the Hall for Cherishing Worthies.

sentences.zh: 起知邛州，未上，改漢州、果州，罷歸。

translations.literal: Raised to serve as prefect of Qiong Prefecture; before assuming office, changed to Han and Guo prefectures; dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Qiongzhou but did not take up the post. He was transferred to Hanzhou and Guozhou, then dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年十二月丙申，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: On bingshen day of the twelfth month of the second year of Chunxi he died, age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the bingshen day of the twelfth month of the second year of Chunxi, at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳苦學，至老不倦，尤工於詩。

translations.literal: Yifeng studied arduously to old age without weariness; he was especially skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Yifeng studied tirelessly to the end of his life and was especially accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 然頗慕晉人簡傲之風，不樂與庸輩接，故平生多蹭蹬，一跌遂不振云。

translations.literal: Yet he quite admired the Jin people's spirit of terse arrogance, did not enjoy associating with mediocre sorts; therefore throughout life he often stumbled; one fall and he did not recover, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he admired the aloof arrogance of Jin-era literati and disliked dealings with mediocre men. His career was therefore often obstructed, and after one fall he never recovered.

sentences.zh: 張孝祥

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoxiang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoxiang

sentences.zh: 張孝祥，字安國，曆陽烏江人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoxiang, styled Anguo, was a man of Wujiang in Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoxiang, styled Anguo, was from Wujiang in Liyang.

sentences.zh: 讀書過一目不忘，下筆頃刻數千言，年十六，領鄉書，再舉冠裏選。

translations.literal: In reading once past the eyes he did not forget; putting brush to paper, in an instant several thousand words; at age sixteen he received the provincial letter; at the second examination he topped the district selection.
translations.idiomatic: He never forgot anything he read. He could write several thousand words in moments. At sixteen he received commendation in the provincial examination, and at his second attempt he topped the district selection.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十四年，廷試第一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing, first in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing he ranked first in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 時策問師友淵源，秦塤與曹冠皆力攻程氏專門之學，孝祥獨不攻。

translations.literal: At the time the policy question asked about the origins of teachers and friends; Qin Kun and Cao Guan both forcefully attacked the Cheng school's specialized learning; Xiaoxiang alone did not attack.
translations.idiomatic: The palace examination question that year concerned teachers and intellectual lineage. Qin Kun and Cao Guan both vigorously attacked the specialized learning of the Cheng school. Xiaoxiang alone did not.

sentences.zh: 考官已定塤冠多士，孝祥次之，曹冠又次之。

translations.literal: The examiners had already ranked Kun first among scholars, Xiaoxiang second, and Cao Guan third.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners had ranked Kun first, Xiaoxiang second, and Cao Guan third.

sentences.zh: 高宗讀塤策皆秦檜語，於是擢孝祥第一，而塤第三，授承事郎、簽書鎮東軍節度判官。

translations.literal: Gaozong reading Kun's policy essay found it all Qin Gui's language; thereupon he elevated Xiaoxiang to first and Kun to third; appointed Gentleman for Meritorious Service and signing secretary military governor's judicial officer of Zhendong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong read Kun's essay and found it echoed Qin Gui's rhetoric throughout. He then placed Xiaoxiang first and Kun third, appointing Xiaoxiang as Gentleman for Meritorious Service and signing secretary under the military governor of Zhendong Army.

sentences.zh: 諭宰相曰：「張栻孝祥詞翰俱美。」

translations.literal: He instructed the chief councilor: "Zhang Shi and Xiaoxiang—both their prose and brushwork are fine."
translations.idiomatic: He told the chief councilor, "Zhang Shi and Xiaoxiang are both accomplished in prose and letters."

sentences.zh: 先是，上之抑塤而擢孝祥也，秦檜已怒，既知孝祥乃祁之子，祁與胡寅厚，檜素憾寅，且唱第後，曹泳揖孝祥於殿庭，以請婚為言，孝祥不答，泳憾之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor lowered Kun and elevated Xiaoxiang, Qin Gui was already angry; once he learned Xiaoxiang was Qi's son, and Qi was close to Hu Yin, and Gui had long resented Yin; moreover after the announcement of ranks, Cao Yong bowed to Xiaoxiang in the palace courtyard and spoke of requesting marriage; Xiaoxiang did not answer; Yong resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor passed over Kun to elevate Xiaoxiang, Qin Gui was already angry. Learning that Xiaoxiang was Qi's son, and that Qi was close to Hu Yin, whom Gui had long resented, Gui's hostility deepened. After the ranking ceremony Cao Yong bowed to Xiaoxiang in the palace courtyard and proposed marriage. Xiaoxiang did not respond, and Yong took offense.

sentences.zh: 於是風言者誣祁有反謀，系詔獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon rumor-mongers falsely accused Qi of having treasonous designs; he was imprisoned in the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: Rumormongers then falsely accused Qi of treason, and he was imprisoned in the edict prison.

sentences.zh: 會檜死，上郊祀之二日，魏良臣密奏散獄釋罪，遂以孝祥為秘書省正字。

translations.literal: When Gui died, on the second day of the emperor's suburban sacrifice Wei Liangchen secretly memorialized to dissolve the prison and release the convicted; thereupon Xiaoxiang was made rectifier of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Gui died, on the second day of the emperor's suburban sacrifice Wei Liangchen secretly memorialized to release the prisoners. Xiaoxiang was then appointed rectifier in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 故事，殿試第一人，次舉始召，孝祥第甫一年得召由此。

translations.literal: By precedent, the first place in the palace examination was summoned at the next examination; Xiaoxiang, only one year after ranking, received summons by this circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the palace examination top graduate was not summoned until the next round of examinations. Xiaoxiang was summoned after only one year because of these events.

sentences.zh: 初對，首言乞總攬權綱以盡更化之美。

translations.literal: At his first audience, he first spoke begging to gather all authority into one hand to fulfill the beauty of the transformation.
translations.idiomatic: At his first audience he asked first that the emperor gather all authority to himself and complete the promise of reform.

sentences.zh: 又言：「官吏忤故相意，並緣文致，有司觀望鍛煉而成罪，乞令有司即改正。」

translations.literal: He again said: "Officials who offended the former chief councilor's intent were all prosecuted by twisted interpretation of the law; the responsible offices looked on and forged evidence to make crimes; I beg that the responsible offices immediately correct this.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Officials who had offended the former chief councilor were prosecuted on fabricated charges. The responsible offices looked on while evidence was forged to secure convictions. I ask that they be ordered to rectify these cases at once.

sentences.zh: 又言：「王安石作《日錄》，一時政事，美則歸己。

translations.literal: He again said: "Wang Anshi compiled the Daily Record; affairs of the time—what was fine he attributed to himself.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Wang Anshi kept a Daily Record in which he claimed credit for every good measure of his day.

sentences.zh: 故相信任之專，非特安石。

translations.literal: Therefore the sovereign's trust in him was exclusive—not only Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sovereign trusted him exclusively—not Wang Anshi alone.

sentences.zh: 臣懼其作《時政記》，亦如安石專用己意，乞取已修《日曆》詳審是正，黜私說以垂無窮。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears that if one compiles Records of Current Policy, it too will like Anshi use only one's own intent; I beg to take the already compiled Calendar, examine it in detail and correct it, and dismiss private interpretations to extend without end."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that if a Record of Current Policy is compiled, it will likewise serve private opinion, as with Anshi. I ask that the Calendar already compiled be carefully reviewed and corrected, and private interpretations removed so that truth may endure.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷校書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Collator.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to collator in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 芝生太廟，孝祥獻文曰《原芝》，以大本未立為言，且言：「芝在仁宗、英宗之室，天意可見，乞早定大計。」

translations.literal: Fungus grew in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Xiaoxiang presented a text called "Inquiry into the Fungus," speaking on the ground that the great foundation was not yet established, and moreover saying: "The fungus appeared in the chambers of Renzong and Yingzong—Heaven's intent can be seen; I beg that the great plan be settled early."
translations.idiomatic: When fungus appeared in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Xiaoxiang submitted "Inquiry into the Fungus," arguing that the succession was not yet secure and that fungus in the halls of Renzong and Yingzong showed Heaven's intent: he begged the throne to settle the great question of the heir at once.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書禮部員外郎，尋為起居舍人、權中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Department of Rites bureau director in the Ministry, and soon became Diarist and Acting Palace Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, then diarist and acting palace secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 初，孝祥登第，出湯思退之門，思退為相，擢孝祥甚峻。

translations.literal: At first, when Xiaoxiang passed the examination, he came from Tang Situi's school; Situi became chief councilor and promoted Xiaoxiang very steeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoxiang first passed the examination he was a protégé of Tang Situi; once Situi became chief councilor he promoted Xiaoxiang with unusual speed.

sentences.zh: 而思退素不喜汪澈，孝祥與澈同為館職，澈老成重厚，而孝祥年少氣銳，往往陵拂之。

translations.literal: Yet Situi had always disliked Wang Che; Xiaoxiang and Che were both in Hanlin posts—Che was mature, weighty, and steady, while Xiaoxiang was young and sharp in spirit and often overbore and brushed him aside.
translations.idiomatic: Situi had always disliked Wang Che. Both served in the Hanlin Academy; Che was mature and steady, while the younger Xiaoxiang was brash and often treated him with condescension.

sentences.zh: 至是澈為御史中丞，首劾孝祥奸不在廬杞下，孝祥遂罷，提舉江州太平興國宮，於是湯思退之客稍稍被逐。

translations.literal: At this time Che became censor-in-chief and was first to impeach Xiaoxiang, saying his treachery was not below Lü Qi's; Xiaoxiang was then dismissed and made intendant of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou—thereupon Situi's clients were gradually driven out.
translations.idiomatic: When Che became censor-in-chief he led the attack, charging that Xiaoxiang's treachery matched Lü Qi's; Xiaoxiang was dismissed to the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou, and Situi's followers were gradually purged.

sentences.zh: 尋除知撫州。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年未三十，蒞事精確，老於州縣者所不及。

translations.literal: Not yet thirty years old, his handling of affairs was precise—veterans of prefectures and counties could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: Though not yet thirty, he administered with a precision veterans of county and prefectural office could not match.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，復集英殿修撰，知平江府。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, he was restored as Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Excellence and made prefect of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong came to the throne he was restored as compiler in the Hall of Assembled Excellence and made prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 事繁劇，孝祥剖決，庭無滯訟。

translations.literal: Affairs were numerous and pressing; Xiaoxiang judged and decided them, and the court had no stalled lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Though affairs were heavy and complex, he decided them swiftly and left no backlog in court.

sentences.zh: 屬邑大姓並海囊橐為奸利，孝祥捕治，籍其家得谷粟數萬。

translations.literal: Great clans in subordinate counties along the sea hoarded wealth for illicit profit; Xiaoxiang arrested and punished them, registered their households, and obtained tens of thousands of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal magnates in his jurisdiction hoarded wealth for illicit profit; he arrested them, confiscated their estates, and seized tens of thousands of bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 明年，吳中大饑，迄賴以濟。

translations.literal: The next year Wu suffered great famine, and in the end relied on this to be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Wu suffered a great famine, the region was saved by that grain.

sentences.zh: 張浚自蜀還朝，薦孝祥，召赴行在。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun returned from Shu to court and recommended Xiaoxiang; he was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun returned from Sichuan he recommended Xiaoxiang, who was summoned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 孝祥既素為湯思退所知，及受浚薦，思退不悅。
