translations.literal: Xiaoxiang had long been known to Tang Situi; when he received Jun's recommendation, Situi was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxiang had long been Situi's protégé, and Situi was displeased when Zhang Jun's recommendation brought him back.

sentences.zh: 孝祥入對，乃陳「二相當同心戮力，以副陛下恢復之志。

translations.literal: Xiaoxiang entered audience and then stated: "The two chief councilors ought to unite hearts and join strength to fulfill Your Majesty's resolve for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Xiaoxiang urged that the two chief councilors unite in purpose to fulfill the emperor's resolve for restoration.

sentences.zh: 且靖康以來惟和戰兩言，遺無窮禍，要先立自治之策以應之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, since Jingkang there have been only the two words peace and war, bequeathing endless calamity—one must first establish a policy of self-governance to respond."
translations.idiomatic: Since Jingkang the court has swung only between peace and war, bequeathing endless trouble; he urged first building a policy of internal self-strengthening.

sentences.zh: 復言：「用才之路太狹，乞博采度外之士以備緩急之用。」

translations.literal: He again said: "The path for employing talent is too narrow; I beg to broadly gather men beyond ordinary measure to prepare for urgent need."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the path to office be widened and exceptional men gathered for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his counsel.

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人，尋除直學士院兼都督府參贊軍事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Secretariat Drafter, and soon made Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies while concurrently Staff Officer for Military Affairs in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace secretariat drafter, then attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies while also staff officer on military affairs in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 俄兼領建康留守，以言者改除敷文閣待制，留守如舊。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently held Jian Kang garrison command; because of critics he was changed to Awaiting Draft in the Hall for Spreading Literature, while retaining garrison command as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also held the Jian Kang garrison command; critics then had him made awaiting draft in the Hall for Spreading Literature while keeping the garrison post.

sentences.zh: 會金再犯邊，孝祥陳金之勢不過欲要盟。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jin again violated the border; Xiaoxiang stated that the Jin's force amounted to no more than wishing to demand a treaty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin again raided the border, Xiaoxiang argued that their aim was only to force a treaty.

sentences.zh: 宣諭使劾孝祥落職，罷。

translations.literal: The edict-delivery commissioner impeached Xiaoxiang for removal from office, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The edict-delivery commissioner impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 復集英殿修撰、知靜江府、廣南西路經略安撫使，治有聲績，復以言者罷。

translations.literal: He was again Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Excellence, prefect of Jingjiang, and Pacification Commissioner of the Guangnan West Circuit; his governance had a reputation for achievement, but again because of critics he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as compiler, made prefect of Jingjiang and pacification commissioner of Guangnan West Circuit, earned a strong administrative reputation, and was again dismissed after criticism.

sentences.zh: 俄起知潭州，為政簡易，時以威濟之，湖南遂以無事。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised to govern Tan Prefecture; his governance was simple and easy, and at times he supplemented it with stern authority—Hunan thus had no incidents.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou, governing with simplicity and ease, sometimes with stern authority, and Hunan remained tranquil.

sentences.zh: 復待制，徙知荊南、荊湖北路安撫使。

translations.literal: He was again made Awaiting Draft and transferred to govern Jingnan while serving as Pacification Commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made awaiting draft and transferred to Jingnan as pacification commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 築寸金堤，自是荊州無水患，置萬盈倉以儲諸漕之運。

translations.literal: He built the Inch-Gold Dike; from then on Jing Prefecture had no flood disaster, and he established the Ten-Thousand-Full Granary to store grain for all transport routes.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Inch-Gold Dike, after which Jingzhou suffered no floods, and established the Ten-Thousand-Full Granary to store grain for transport routes.

sentences.zh: 請祠，以疾卒，孝宗惜之，有用才不盡之歎。

translations.literal: He requested a shrine appointment; he died of illness; Xiaozong regretted him and sighed that his talent had not been fully used.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a sinecure but died of illness; Xiaozong mourned the waste of his talent.

sentences.zh: 進顯謨閣直學士致仕，年三十八。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Academician of the Hall of Manifest Strategy and retired, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously advanced to academician of the Hall of Manifest Strategy and had retired at thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 孝祥俊逸，文章過人，尤工翰墨，嘗親書奏劄，高宗見之，曰：「必將名世。」

translations.literal: Xiaoxiang was handsome and free-spirited; his writing surpassed others, and he was especially skilled in calligraphy; he once personally wrote a memorial, and Gaozong saw it and said: "He will surely make a name in the world."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxiang was brilliant and free-spirited, his prose exceptional and his calligraphy especially fine; when Gaozong saw a memorial he had written in his own hand, he said, "This man will surely leave his mark on the age."

sentences.zh: 但渡江初，大議惟和戰，張浚主復仇，湯思退祖秦檜之說力主和，孝祥出入二人之門而兩持其說，議者惜之。

translations.literal: Yet at the beginning after crossing the river, the great debate was only peace and war—Zhang Jun upheld revenge, Tang Situi followed Qin Gui's doctrine and strongly upheld peace; Xiaoxiang moved in and out of both men's circles and held both views, and critics regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the early years after the move south the great debate was peace versus war: Zhang Jun urged revenge, Tang Situi followed Qin Gui in pressing for peace, and Xiaoxiang moved between both camps, holding to both sides—commentators regretted the inconsistency.

sentences.zh: 論曰：尤袤學本程頤，所謂老成典刑者，立朝抗論，與人主爭是非，不允不已，而能令終完節，難矣。

translations.literal: The critique says: You Mao's learning took Cheng Yi as root—what is called mature precedent and model statute; standing at court he resisted in argument, contending right and wrong with the sovereign, not stopping until refused, yet able to end his life with integrity intact—this is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: You Mao's learning derived from Cheng Yi; he was a mature exemplar of public morals who remonstrated at court, disputing right and wrong with his sovereign until overruled, yet finished his life with integrity intact—a rare achievement.

sentences.zh: 謝諤、顏師魯、袁樞臨民則以治辨聞，立朝則啟沃忠諫，各舉乃職，為世師表。

translations.literal: Xie E, Yan Shilu, and Yuan Shu, in governing the people were known for orderly administration; at court they nourished with loyal remonstrance—each performed his office and served as a model for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xie E, Yan Shilu, and Yuan Shu were famed for orderly local government and loyal remonstrance at court; each fulfilled his duty and stood as a model for their age.

sentences.zh: 李椿、劉儀鳳言論節概，著於行事。

translations.literal: Li Chun and Liu Yifeng's words and conduct showed principled integrity, manifest in their actions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chun and Liu Yifeng showed their principled integrity in word and deed.

sentences.zh: 張孝祥早負才畯，蒞政揚聲，迨其兩持和戰，君子每歎息焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoxiang early bore outstanding talent; in office he raised his reputation, but when he held both peace and war, gentlemen often sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoxiang displayed exceptional talent early and won fame in office, yet gentlemen sighed when he straddled the camps of peace and war.
